मनसा वचसा साक्षात्कर्मणा पतिभावतः ।
सत्यं ब्रवीमि नोऽसत्यं संवृतः शङ्करो मया ॥
3.33.m: In mind, in speech, and directly in action, regarding him as my husband— / I speak the truth, not a lie—Śaṅkara has been chosen by me.

3.33.s:
jānāmi durlabhaṃ vastu kathaṃ prāpyaṃ mayā bhavet |
tathāpi manasautsukyāttapyate me tapo'dhunā ||
3.33.d:
जानामि दुर्लभं वस्तु कथं प्राप्यं मया भवेत् ।
तथापि मनसौत्सुक्यात्तप्यते मे तपोऽधुना ॥
3.33.m: I know he is a rare object, and how could he be obtained by me? / Even so, out of mental longing, my austerity is now being performed.

3.33.s:
hitvendrapramukhāndevānviṣṇuṃ brahmāṇamapyaham |
patiṃ pinākapāṇiṃ vai prāptumicchāmi satyataḥ ||
3.33.d:
हित्वेन्द्रप्रमुखान्देवान्विष्णुं ब्रह्माणमप्यहम् ।
पतिं पिनाकपाणिं वै प्राप्तुमिच्छामि सत्यतः ॥
3.33.m: Setting aside the gods led by Indra, and even Viṣṇu and Brahmā, / I truly wish to obtain the wielder of the Pināka bow as my husband."

3.33.s:
nandīśvara uvāca |
ityevaṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā pārvatyā hi suniścitam |
mune sa jaṭilo rudro vihasanvākyamabravīt ||
3.33.d:
नन्दीश्वर उवाच ।
इत्येवं वचनं श्रुत्वा पार्वत्या हि सुनिश्चितम् ।
मुने स जटिलो रुद्रो विहसन्वाक्यमब्रवीत् ॥
3.33.m: Nandīśvara said: / Having heard these resolute words of Pārvatī, / that Rudra with matted hair laughed and spoke words, O sage.

3.33.s:
jaṭila uvāca |
himācalasute devi kā buddhiḥ svīkṛtā tvayā |
rudrārthaṃ vibudhānhitvā karoṣi vipulaṃ tapaḥ ||
3.33.d:
जटिल उवाच ।
हिमाचलसुते देवि का बुद्धिः स्वीकृता त्वया ।
रुद्रार्थं विबुधान्हित्वा करोषि विपुलं तपः ॥
3.33.m: The ascetic with matted hair said: / "O goddess, daughter of the Himālaya, what sort of idea have you embraced? / Forsaking the gods, you perform immense austerity for the sake of Rudra!

3.33.s:
jānāmyahaṃ ca taṃ rudraṃ śṛṇu tvaṃ pravadāmi te |
vṛṣadhvajaḥ sa rudro hi vikṛtātmā jaṭādharaḥ ||
3.33.d:
जानाम्यहं च तं रुद्रं शृणु त्वं प्रवदामि ते ।
वृषध्वजः स रुद्रो हि विकृतात्मा जटाधरः ॥
3.33.m: I know that Rudra; listen, I shall tell you: / that Rudra has a bull on his banner, a deformed nature, and wears matted hair.

3.33.s:
ekākī ca sadā nityaṃ virāgī ca viśeṣataḥ |
tasmāttvaṃ tena rudreṇa mano yoktuṃ na cārhasi ||
3.33.d:
एकाकी च सदा नित्यं विरागी च विशेषतः ।
तस्मात्त्वं तेन रुद्रेण मनो योक्तुं न चार्हसि ॥
3.33.m: He is always solitary and exceedingly detached; / therefore you ought not to set your heart upon that Rudra.

3.33.s:
sarvaṃ viruddhaṃ rūpādi tava devi harasya ca |
mahyaṃ na rocate hyetadyadīcchasi tathā kuru ||
3.33.d:
सर्वं विरुद्धं रूपादि तव देवि हरस्य च ।
मह्यं न रोचते ह्येतद्यदीच्छसि तथा कुरु ॥
3.33.m: Everything—beauty and the rest—is contrary between you, O goddess, and Hara. / This does not please me at all; if you still wish it, do as you please."

3.33.s:
nandīśvara uvāca |
ityuktvā ca punā rudro brahmacārisvarūpavān |
nininda bahudhātmānaṃ tadagre tāṃ parīkṣitum ||
3.33.d:
नन्दीश्वर उवाच ।
इत्युक्त्वा च पुना रुद्रो ब्रह्मचारिस्वरूपवान् ।
निनिन्द बहुधात्मानं तदग्रे तां परीक्षितुम् ॥
3.33.m: Nandīśvara said: / Having spoken thus, Rudra, in the form of a celibate student, / reviled himself in many ways before her in order to test her.

3.33.s:
tacchrutvā pārvatī devī vipravākyaṃ durāsadam |
pratyuvāca mahākruddhā śivanindāparaṃ ca tam ||
3.33.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा पार्वती देवी विप्रवाक्यं दुरासदम् ।
प्रत्युवाच महाक्रुद्धा शिवनिन्दापरं च तम् ॥
3.33.m: Hearing that harsh speech of the brahmin, the goddess Pārvatī / became exceedingly angry and replied to him who was intent on reviling Śiva:

3.33.s:
etāvaddhi mayā jñātaṃ kaścid dhanyo bhaviṣyati |
parantu sakalaṃ jñātamavadhyo dṛśyate'dhunā ||
3.33.d:
एतावद्धि मया ज्ञातं कश्चिद् धन्यो भविष्यति ।
परन्तु सकलं ज्ञातमवध्यो दृश्यतेऽधुना ॥
3.33.m: “I thought this much: ‘He must be some blessed person.’ / But now everything is known; you appear [merely] someone not to be killed.

3.33.s:
brahmacārisvarūpeṇa kaścittvaṃ dhūrta āgataḥ |
śivanindā kṛtā mūḍha tvayā manyurabhūnmama ||
3.33.d:
ब्रह्मचारिस्वरूपेण कश्चित्त्वं धूर्त आगतः ।
शिवनिन्दा कृता मूढ त्वया मन्युरभून्मम ॥
3.33.m: You are some rogue who has arrived in the form of a celibate student! / You have reviled Śiva, you fool, and caused me anger.

3.33.s:
śivaṃ tvaṃ ca na jānāsi śivāttvaṃ hi bahirmukhaḥ |
tvatpūjā ca kṛtā yanme tasmāttāpayutābhavam ||
3.33.d:
शिवं त्वं च न जानासि शिवात्त्वं हि बहिर्मुखः ।
त्वत्पूजा च कृता यन्मे तस्मात्तापयुताभवम् ॥
3.33.m: You do not know Śiva, for you are turned away from Śiva. / Because worship was offered to you by me, I have come to feel torment.

3.33.s:
śivanindāṃ karotīha tattvamajñāya yaḥ pumān |
ājanmasañcitaṃ puṇyaṃ tasya bhasmībhavatyuta ||
3.33.d:
शिवनिन्दां करोतीह तत्त्वमज्ञाय यः पुमान् ।
आजन्मसञ्चितं पुण्यं तस्य भस्मीभवत्युत ॥
3.33.m: Whatever man in this world reviles Śiva without knowing reality, / even the merit accumulated since his birth turns to ashes.

3.33.s: śivavidveṣiṇaṃ spṛṣṭvā prāyaścittaṃ samācaret ||
3.33.d: शिवविद्वेषिणं स्पृष्ट्वा प्रायश्चित्तं समाचरेत् ॥
3.33.m: Having touched one who hates Śiva, one should perform an expiation.

3.33.s:
re re duṣṭa tvayā proktamahaṃ jānāmi śaṅkaram |
niścayena na vijñātaḥ śiva eva paraḥ prabhuḥ ||
3.33.d:
रे रे दुष्ट त्वया प्रोक्तमहं जानामि शङ्करम् ।
निश्चयेन न विज्ञातः शिव एव परः प्रभुः ॥
3.33.m: Hey, wicked one, you said: ‘I know Śaṅkara.’ / But certainly you do not know that Śiva alone is the supreme Lord.

3.33.s:
yathā tathā bhavedrudro māyayā bahurūpavān |
mamābhīṣṭaprado'tyantaṃ nirvikāraḥ satāṃ priyaḥ ||
3.33.d:
यथा तथा भवेद्रुद्रो मायया बहुरूपवान् ।
ममाभीष्टप्रदोऽत्यन्तं निर्विकारः सतां प्रियः ॥
3.33.m: Be Rudra as he may, multi-formed by means of māyā, / he grants my deepest desire, is entirely changeless, and is dear to the virtuous.

3.33.s:
nandīśvara uvāca |
ityuktvā taṃ śivā devī śivatattvaṃ jagāda sā |
yatra brahmatayā rudraḥ kathyate nirguṇo'vyayaḥ ||
3.33.d:
नन्दीश्वर उवाच ।
इत्युक्त्वा तं शिवा देवी शिवतत्त्वं जगाद सा ।
यत्र ब्रह्मतया रुद्रः कथ्यते निर्गुणोऽव्ययः ॥
3.33.m: Nandīśvara said: / Having spoken thus to him, the goddess Śivā declared the reality of Śiva, / wherein Rudra is declared to be Brahman, devoid of qualities and imperishable.

3.33.s:
tadākarṇya vaco devyā brahmacārī sa vai dvijaḥ |
punarvacanamādātuṃ yāvadeva pracakrame ||
3.33.d:
तदाकर्ण्य वचो देव्या ब्रह्मचारी स वै द्विजः ।
पुनर्वचनमादातुं यावदेव प्रचक्रमे ॥
3.33.m: Hearing those words of the goddess, that twice-born celibate student, / just as he began to speak again,

3.33.s:
provāca girijā tāvatsvasakhīṃ vijayāṃ drutam |
śivāsaktamanovṛttiḥ śivanindāparāṅmukhī ||
3.33.d:
प्रोवाच गिरिजा तावत्स्वसखीं विजयां द्रुतम् ।
शिवासक्तमनोवृत्तिः शिवनिन्दापराङ्मुखी ॥
3.33.m: the mountain-born goddess quickly spoke to her friend Vijayā, / her mind's operation fixed on Śiva, averse to the reviling of Śiva.

3.33.s:
girijovāca |
vāraṇīyaḥ prayatnena sakhyayaṃ hi dvijādhamaḥ |
punarvaktumanāścāyaṃ śivanindāṃ kariṣyati ||
3.33.d:
गिरिजोवाच ।
वारणीयः प्रयत्नेन सख्ययं हि द्विजाधमः ।
पुनर्वक्तुमनाश्चायं शिवनिन्दां करिष्यति ॥
3.33.m: The mountain-born goddess said: / “O friend, this lowest of the twice-born must be stopped with effort, / for he intends to speak again and will revile Śiva.

3.33.s:
na kevalaṃ bhavetpāpaṃ nindākartuḥ śivasya hi |
yo vai śṛṇoti tannindāṃ pāpabhāksa bhavediha ||
3.33.d:
न केवलं भवेत्पापं निन्दाकर्तुः शिवस्य हि ।
यो वै शृणोति तन्निन्दां पापभाक्स भवेदिह ॥
3.33.m: Not only does sin accrue to the slanderer of Śiva, / but whoever hears his slander also partakes of sin in this world.

3.33.s:
śivanindākaro vadhyaḥ sarvathā śivakiṅkaraiḥ |
brāhmaṇaścetsa vai tyājyo gantavyaṃ tatsthalāddrutam ||
3.33.d:
शिवनिन्दाकरो वध्यः सर्वथा शिवकिङ्करैः ।
ब्राह्मणश्चेत्स वै त्याज्यो गन्तव्यं तत्स्थलाद्द्रुतम् ॥
3.33.m: The slanderer of Śiva is to be slain by all means by Śiva’s attendants; / but if he is a brahmin, he must be abandoned, and one must go quickly from that place.

3.33.s:
ayaṃ duṣṭaḥ punarnindāṃ kariṣyati śivasya hi |
brāhmaṇatvādavadhyaśca tyājyo'dṛśyaśca sarvathā ||
3.33.d:
अयं दुष्टः पुनर्निन्दां करिष्यति शिवस्य हि ।
ब्राह्मणत्वादवध्यश्च त्याज्योऽदृश्यश्च सर्वथा ॥
3.33.m: This wicked one will revile Śiva again; / because he is a brahmin he must not be killed, but must be abandoned and never looked upon.

3.33.s:
sthalametad drutaṃ hitvā yāsyāmo'nyatra mā ciram |
yathā sambhāṣaṇaṃ na syādanenāviduṣā punaḥ ||
3.33.d:
स्थलमेतद् द्रुतं हित्वा यास्यामोऽन्यत्र मा चिरम् ।
यथा सम्भाषणं न स्यादनेनाविदुषा पुनः ॥
3.33.m: Leaving this place quickly, let us go elsewhere without delay, / so that there will be no further conversation with this ignorant fool.”

3.33.s:
nandīśvara uvāca |
ityuktvā comayā yāvatpadamutkṣipyate mune |
asau tāvacchivaḥ sākṣādālalambe paṭaṃ svayam ||
3.33.d:
नन्दीश्वर उवाच ।
इत्युक्त्वा चोमया यावत्पदमुत्क्षिप्यते मुने ।
असौ तावच्छिवः साक्षादाललम्बे पटं स्वयम् ॥
3.33.m: Nandīśvara said: / Having spoken thus, O sage, just as a step was being raised by Umā, / right then Śiva in person took hold of her garment himself.

3.33.s:
kṛtvā svarūpaṃ divyaṃ ca śivādhyānaṃ yathā tathā |
darśayitvā śivāyai tāmuvācāvāṅmukhīṃ śivaḥ ||
3.33.d:
कृत्वा स्वरूपं दिव्यं च शिवाध्यानं यथा तथा ।
दर्शयित्वा शिवायै तामुवाचावाङ्मुखीं शिवः ॥
3.33.m: Assuming his divine form, exactly as in meditation upon Śiva, / and revealing it to Śivā, Śiva spoke to her as she stood with her face cast down.

3.33.s:
śiva uvāca |
kutra tvaṃ yāsi māṃ hitvā na tvaṃ tyājyā mayā śive |
mayā parīkṣitāsi tvaṃ dṛḍhabhaktāsi me'naghe ||
3.33.d:
शिव उवाच ।
कुत्र त्वं यासि मां हित्वा न त्वं त्याज्या मया शिवे ।
मया परीक्षितासि त्वं दृढभक्तासि मेऽनघे ॥
3.33.m: Śiva said: / “Where are you going, abandoning me? You are not to be abandoned by me, O Śivā! / You have been tested by me; you are firmly devoted to me, O sinless one.

3.33.s:
brahmacārisvarūpeṇa bhāvamicchustvadīyakam |
tavopakaṇṭhamāgatya prāvocaṃ vividhaṃ vacaḥ ||
3.33.d:
ब्रह्मचारिस्वरूपेण भावमिच्छुस्त्वदीयकम् ।
तवोपकण्ठमागत्य प्रावोचं विविधं वचः ॥
3.33.m: Desiring to know your state of mind under the form of a celibate student, / I approached you and spoke various words.

3.33.s:
prasanno'smi dṛḍhaṃ bhaktyā śive tava viśeṣataḥ |
cittepsitaṃ varaṃ brūhi nādeyaṃ vidyate tava ||
3.33.d:
प्रसन्नोऽस्मि दृढं भक्त्या शिवे तव विशेषतः ।
चित्तेप्सितं वरं ब्रूहि नादेयं विद्यते तव ॥
3.33.m: I am deeply pleased with your devotion, O Śivā, especially so. / Name the boon desired in your heart; there is nothing not to be given to you.

3.33.s:
adyaprabhṛti te dāsastapobhiḥ premanirbhare |
kṛto'smi tava saundaryātkṣaṇa eko yugāyate ||
3.33.d:
अद्यप्रभृति ते दासस्तपोभिः प्रेमनिर्भरे ।
कृतोऽस्मि तव सौन्दर्यात्क्षण एको युगायते ॥
3.33.m: From this day forth I am your servant, bought by your austerities, O woman filled with love! / Because of your beauty, a single moment feels like an aeon.

3.33.s:
tyajyatāṃ ca tvayā lajjā mama patnī sanātanī |
ehi priye tvayā sākaṃ drutaṃ yāmi svakaṃ girim ||
3.33.d:
त्यज्यतां च त्वया लज्जा मम पत्नी सनातनी ।
एहि प्रिये त्वया साकं द्रुतं यामि स्वकं गिरिम् ॥
3.33.m: Cast away your shyness; you are my eternal wife. / Come, my beloved, together with you I will go quickly to my mountain.”

3.33.s:
ityuktavati deveśe śivātimudamāpa sā |
tapoduḥkhaṃ tu yatsarvaṃ tajjahau drutameva hi ||
3.33.d:
इत्युक्तवति देवेशे शिवातिमुदमाप सा ।
तपोदुःखं तु यत्सर्वं तज्जहौ द्रुतमेव हि ॥
3.33.m: When the Lord of Gods had spoken thus, Śivā attained immense joy; / whatever distress had arisen from her austerity, she immediately abandoned it all.

3.33.s:
tataḥ prahṛṣṭā sā dṛṣṭvā divyarūpaṃ śivasya tat |
pratyuvāca prabhuṃ prītyā lajjayādhomukhī śivā ||
3.33.d:
ततः प्रहृष्टा सा दृष्ट्वा दिव्यरूपं शिवस्य तत् ।
प्रत्युवाच प्रभुं प्रीत्या लज्जयाधोमुखी शिवा ॥
3.33.m: Then, delighted upon seeing that divine form of Śiva, / the auspicious goddess, her face downcast with bashfulness, replied to the Lord with love.

3.33.s:
śivovāca |
yadi prasanno deveśa karoṣi ca kṛpāṃ mayi |
patirme bhava deveśa ityuktaḥ śivayā śivaḥ ||
3.33.d:
शिवोवाच ।
यदि प्रसन्नो देवेश करोषि च कृपां मयि ।
पतिर्मे भव देवेश इत्युक्तः शिवया शिवः ॥
3.33.m: Śivā said: / “If you are pleased, O Lord of Gods, and show grace to me, / become my husband, O Lord of Gods.” Thus was Śiva addressed by Śivā.

3.33.s:
nandīśvara uvāca
gṛhītvā vidhivatpāṇiṃ kailāsaṃ sa tayā yayau |
patiṃ taṃ girijā prāpya devakāryaṃ cakāra sā ||
3.33.d:
नन्दीश्वर उवाच
गृहीत्वा विधिवत्पाणिं कैलासं स तया ययौ ।
पतिं तं गिरिजा प्राप्य देवकार्यं चकार सा ॥
3.33.m: Nandīśvara said: / Taking her hand according to the prescribed rules, he went with her to Kailāsa. / Having obtained him as her husband, the mountain-born goddess accomplished the mission of the gods.

3.33.s:
iti proktastu te tāta brahmacārisvarūpakaḥ |
śivāvatāro hi mayā śivābhāvaparīkṣakaḥ ||
3.33.d:
इति प्रोक्तस्तु ते तात ब्रह्मचारिस्वरूपकः ।
शिवावतारो हि मया शिवाभावपरीक्षकः ॥
3.33.m: Thus, dear one, has been told to you by me the incarnation of Śiva / in the form of a celibate student, which tested the devotion of Śivā.

3.33.s:
idamākhyānamanaghaṃ paramaṃ vyāhṛtaṃ mayā |
ya etacchṛṇuyātprītyā sa sukhī gatimāpnuyāt ||
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ||
śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
śrīśivamahāpurāṇam ||
tṛtīyāyāṃ śatarudrasaṃhitāyāṃ
3.33.d:
इदमाख्यानमनघं परमं व्याहृतं मया ।
य एतच्छृणुयात्प्रीत्या स सुखी गतिमाप्नुयात् ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः ॥
श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ॥
तृतीयायां शतरुद्रसंहितायां
3.33.m:
This supreme, stainless narrative has been related by me; / whoever hears this with love will become happy and attain the supreme destination.

Thus ends the thirty-third chapter, named ‘Description of the Celibate Student Incarnation of Śiva,’ in the third book, the Śatarudrasaṃhitā, of the glorious Śiva Mahāpurāṇa.

3.34.s:
nandīśvara uvāca |
sanatkumāra sarvajña śivasya paramātmanaḥ |
avatāraṃ śṛṇu vibhoḥ sunartakanaṭāhvayam ||
3.34.d:
नन्दीश्वर उवाच ।
सनत्कुमार सर्वज्ञ शिवस्य परमात्मनः ।
अवतारं शृणु विभोः सुनर्तकनटाह्वयम् ॥
3.34.m: Nandīśvara said: / O omniscient Sanatkumāra, hear of the incarnation of the all-pervading Śiva, / the Supreme Self, known by the name of the Good Dancer and Actor.

3.34.s:
yadā hi kālikā devī pārvatī himavatsutā |
tepe tapaḥ suvimalaṃ vanaṃ gatvā śivāptaye ||
3.34.d:
यदा हि कालिका देवी पार्वती हिमवत्सुता ।
तेपे तपः सुविमलं वनं गत्वा शिवाप्तये ॥
3.34.m: When the goddess Kālikā, Pārvatī, daughter of the Himavat, / went to the forest and performed flawless austerity in order to attain Śiva,

3.34.s:
tadā śivaḥ prasanno'bhūttasyāḥ sutapaso mune |
tadvṛttasuparīkṣārthaṃ varaṃ dātuṃ mudā yayau ||
3.34.d:
तदा शिवः प्रसन्नोऽभूत्तस्याः सुतपसो मुने ।
तद्वृत्तसुपरीक्षार्थं वरं दातुं मुदा ययौ ॥
3.34.m: then Śiva became pleased by her excellent austerity, O sage, / and went joyfully to grant a boon in order to thoroughly test her conduct.

3.34.s:
svarūpaṃ darśayāmāsa tasyai suprītamānasaḥ |
varaṃ brūhīti covāca tāṃ śivāṃ śaṅkaro mune ||
3.34.d:
स्वरूपं दर्शयामास तस्यै सुप्रीतमानसः ।
वरं ब्रूहीति चोवाच तां शिवां शङ्करो मुने ॥
3.34.m: With an exceedingly delighted mind, he displayed his form to her / and said to that auspicious goddess: “Choose a boon,” O sage.

3.34.s:
tacchrutvā śambhuvacanaṃ dṛṣṭvā tadrūpamuttamam |
sujaharṣa śivātīva prāha taṃ supraṇamya sā ||
3.34.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा शम्भुवचनं दृष्ट्वा तद्रूपमुत्तमम् ।
सुजहर्ष शिवातीव प्राह तं सुप्रणम्य सा ॥
3.34.m: Hearing that speech of Śambhu and seeing that supreme form, / Śivā rejoiced exceedingly, and bowing respectfully to him, she said:

3.34.s:
pārvatyuvāca |
yadi prasanno deveśa mahyaṃ deyo varo yadi |
patirbhava mameśāna kṛpāṃ kuru mamopari ||
3.34.d:
पार्वत्युवाच ।
यदि प्रसन्नो देवेश मह्यं देयो वरो यदि ।
पतिर्भव ममेशान कृपां कुरु ममोपरि ॥
3.34.m: Pārvatī said: / “If you are pleased, O Lord of Gods, if a boon is to be given to me, / become my husband, O Īśāna; bestow grace upon me.

3.34.s:
piturgṛhe mayā samyaggamyate tvadanujñayā |
gantavyaṃ bhavatā nātha matpituḥ pārśvataḥ prabho ||
3.34.d:
पितुर्गृहे मया सम्यग्गम्यते त्वदनुज्ञया ।
गन्तव्यं भवता नाथ मत्पितुः पार्श्वतः प्रभो ॥
3.34.m: With your permission I will proceed duly to my father’s house; / you must come, O Lord, to the presence of my father, O Master.

3.34.s:
yācasva māṃ tato bhikṣuḥ khyāpayaṃśca yaśaḥ śubham |
piturme saphalaṃ sarvaṃ kuru prītyā gṛhāśramam ||
3.34.d:
याचस्व मां ततो भिक्षुः ख्यापयंश्च यशः शुभम् ।
पितुर्मे सफलं सर्वं कुरु प्रीत्या गृहाश्रमम् ॥
3.34.m: Then, as a mendicant, ask for me, making known your auspicious fame; / joyfully make the householder life of my father entirely fruitful.

3.34.s:
tato yathoktavidhinā kartumarhasi bho prabho |
vivāhaṃ tvaṃ maheśāna devānāṃ kāryasiddhaye ||
3.34.d:
ततो यथोक्तविधिना कर्तुमर्हसि भो प्रभो ।
विवाहं त्वं महेशान देवानां कार्यसिद्धये ॥
3.34.m: Then, O Master, O Maheśāna, you should perform / the marriage in accordance with the prescribed injunctions for the accomplishment of the purpose of the gods.

3.34.s:
kāmaṃ me pūraya vibho nirvikāro bhavānsadā |
bhaktavatsalanāmā hi tava bhaktāsmyahaṃ sadā ||
3.34.d:
कामं मे पूरय विभो निर्विकारो भवान्सदा ।
भक्तवत्सलनामा हि तव भक्तास्म्यहं सदा ॥
3.34.m: Fulfill my desire, O all-pervading Lord; you are ever free from transformation; / indeed, your name is affectionate toward devotees, and I am ever your devotee.”

3.34.s:
nandīśvara uvāca |
ityuktaḥ sa tayā śambhurmaheśo bhaktavatsalaḥ |
tathāstviti vacaḥ procyāntarhitaḥ svagiriṃ yayau ||
3.34.d:
नन्दीश्वर उवाच ।
इत्युक्तः स तया शम्भुर्महेशो भक्तवत्सलः ।
तथास्त्विति वचः प्रोच्यान्तर्हितः स्वगिरिं ययौ ॥
3.34.m: Nandīśvara said: / Thus addressed by her, Śambhu, the great Lord affectionate toward devotees, / said, “So be it,” and vanishing, went to his own mountain.

3.34.s:
pārvatyapi tataḥ prītyā svasakhībhyāṃ samanvitā |
jagāma svapiturgehaṃ rūpaṃ kṛtvā tu sārthakam ||
3.34.d:
पार्वत्यपि ततः प्रीत्या स्वसखीभ्यां समन्विता ।
जगाम स्वपितुर्गेहं रूपं कृत्वा तु सार्थकम् ॥
3.34.m: Pārvatī, too, accompanied by her two friends, then joyfully / went to her father’s home, having made her beauty purposeful.

3.34.s:
pārvatyāgamanaṃ śrutvā menayā sa himācalaḥ |
parivārayuto draṣṭuṃ svasutāṃ tāṃ yayau mudā ||
3.34.d:
पार्वत्यागमनं श्रुत्वा मेनया स हिमाचलः ।
परिवारयुतो द्रष्टुं स्वसुतां तां ययौ मुदा ॥
3.34.m: Hearing of Pārvatī’s arrival, the Himācala together with Menā / and accompanied by his retinue went joyfully to see his daughter.

3.34.s:
dṛṣṭvā tāṃ suprasannāsyāmānayāmāsaturgṛham |
kārayāmāsatuḥ prītyā mahānandau mahotsavam ||
3.34.d:
दृष्ट्वा तां सुप्रसन्नास्यामानयामासतुर्गृहम् ।
कारयामासतुः प्रीत्या महानन्दौ महोत्सवम् ॥
3.34.m: Seeing her whose face was bright with joy, they both brought her home, / and, filled with great bliss, they lovingly held a great festival.

3.34.s:
dhanaṃ dadau dvijādibhyo menā girivarastathā |
maṅgalaṃ kārayāmāsa savedadhvanimādarāt ||
3.34.d:
धनं ददौ द्विजादिभ्यो मेना गिरिवरस्तथा ।
मङ्गलं कारयामास सवेदध्वनिमादरात् ॥
3.34.m: Menā and the excellent mountain gave wealth to the twice-born and others, / and respectfully caused auspicious rites to be performed with the sound of the Vedas.

3.34.s:
tataḥ svakanyayā sārdhamuvāsa prāṅgaṇe mudā |
menā ca himavāñchailaḥ snātuṃ gaṅgāṃ jagāma saḥ ||
3.34.d:
ततः स्वकन्यया सार्धमुवास प्राङ्गणे मुदा ।
मेना च हिमवाञ्छैलः स्नातुं गङ्गां जगाम सः ॥
3.34.m: Then Menā sat joyfully with her daughter in the courtyard, / and that mountain Himavat went to the Gaṅgā to bathe.

3.34.s:
etasminnantare śambhuḥ sulīlo bhaktavatsalaḥ |
sunartakanaṭo bhūtvā menakāsannidhiṃ yayau ||
3.34.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे शम्भुः सुलीलो भक्तवत्सलः ।
सुनर्तकनटो भूत्वा मेनकासन्निधिं ययौ ॥
3.34.m: In the meantime, Śambhu, fond of divine sport and affectionate toward devotees, / became an expert dancer and actor, and approached Menakā.

3.34.s:
śṛṅgaṃ vāme kare dhṛtvā dakṣiṇe ḍamaruṃ tathā |
pṛṣṭhe kanthāṃ raktavāsā nṛtyagānaviśāradaḥ ||
3.34.d:
शृङ्गं वामे करे धृत्वा दक्षिणे डमरुं तथा ।
पृष्ठे कन्थां रक्तवासा नृत्यगानविशारदः ॥
3.34.m: Holding a horn in his left hand and a ḍamaru drum in his right, / wearing a patched cloth on his back and red garments, he was skilled in dancing and singing.

3.34.s:
tatastu naṭarūpo'sau menakāprāṅgaṇe mudā |
cakre sa nṛtyaṃ vividhaṃ gānaṃ cāti manoharam ||
3.34.d:
ततस्तु नटरूपोऽसौ मेनकाप्राङ्गणे मुदा ।
चक्रे स नृत्यं विविधं गानं चाति मनोहरम् ॥
3.34.m: Then, in the form of a dancer, in Menakā’s courtyard, / he joyfully performed various dances and extremely charming singing.

3.34.s:
śṛṅgañca ḍamaruṃ tatra vādayāmāsa sudhvanim |
mahotiṃ vividhāṃ prītyā sa cakāra manoharām ||
3.34.d:
शृङ्गञ्च डमरुं तत्र वादयामास सुध्वनिम् ।
महोतिं विविधां प्रीत्या स चकार मनोहराम् ॥
3.34.m: He played the horn and the ḍamaru drum there with a sweet sound; / with delight he performed various captivating sports.

3.34.s:
taṃ draṣṭuṃ nāgarāḥ sarve puruṣāśca striyastathā |
ājagmuḥ sahasā tatra bālā vṛddhā api dhruvam ||
3.34.d:
तं द्रष्टुं नागराः सर्वे पुरुषाश्च स्त्रियस्तथा ।
आजग्मुः सहसा तत्र बाला वृद्धा अपि ध्रुवम् ॥
3.34.m: To see him, all the townsfolk, both men and women, / suddenly came there, surely including children and old folk as well.

3.34.s:
śrutvā sugītaṃ taṃ dṛṣṭvā sunṛtyaṃ ca manoharam |
sahasā mumuhuḥ sarve menāpi ca tadā mune ||
3.34.d:
श्रुत्वा सुगीतं तं दृष्ट्वा सुनृत्यं च मनोहरम् ।
सहसा मुमुहुः सर्वे मेनापि च तदा मुने ॥
3.34.m: Hearing his melodious singing and beholding his charming, fine dance, / they all suddenly fell into wonder, and so did Menā at that time, O sage.

3.34.s:
tato menāśu ratnāni svarṇapātrasthitāni ca |
tasmai dātuṃ yayau prītyā tadūtiprītamānasā ||
3.34.d:
ततो मेनाशु रत्नानि स्वर्णपात्रस्थितानि च ।
तस्मै दातुं ययौ प्रीत्या तदूतिप्रीतमानसा ॥
3.34.m: Then Menā, her mind pleased by his sport, quickly went with joy / to give him jewels placed upon a golden plate.

3.34.s:
tāni na svīcakārāsau bhikṣāṃ kāṅkṣe śivāṃ ca tām |
punaḥ sunṛtyaṃ gānaṃ ca kautukātkartumudyataḥ ||
3.34.d:
तानि न स्वीचकारासौ भिक्षां काङ्क्षे शिवां च ताम् ।
पुनः सुनृत्यं गानं च कौतुकात्कर्तुमुद्यतः ॥
3.34.m: He did not accept them, [saying,] “I desire Śivā as alms,” / and again eagerly prepared to perform a fine dance and song out of sport.

3.34.s:
menā tadvacanaṃ śrutvā cukopāti suvismitā |
bhikṣukaṃ bhartsayāmāsa bahiṣkartumiyeṣa sā ||
3.34.d:
मेना तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा चुकोपाति सुविस्मिता ।
भिक्षुकं भर्त्सयामास बहिष्कर्तुमियेष सा ॥
3.34.m: Hearing his words, Menā became extremely angry and greatly astonished; / she scolded the beggar and wished to throw him out.

3.34.s:
etasminnantare tatra gaṅgāto girirāḍ yayau |
dadarśa purato bhikṣuṃ prāṅgaṇasthaṃ narākṛtim ||
3.34.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे तत्र गङ्गातो गिरिराड् ययौ ।
ददर्श पुरतो भिक्षुं प्राङ्गणस्थं नराकृतिम् ॥
3.34.m: In the meantime, the king of mountains came there from the Gaṅgā; / he saw before him in the courtyard the beggar in human form.

3.34.s:
śrutvā menāmukhād vṛttaṃ tatsarvaṃ sucukopa saḥ |
ājñāṃ cakārānucarānbahiḥ kartuṃ ca bhikṣukam ||
3.34.d:
श्रुत्वा मेनामुखाद् वृत्तं तत्सर्वं सुचुकोप सः ।
आज्ञां चकारानुचरान्बहिः कर्तुं च भिक्षुकम् ॥
3.34.m: Hearing that whole report from Menā’s mouth, he became very angry; / he commanded his servants to cast the beggar outside.

3.34.s:
mahāgnimiva duḥsparśaṃ prajvalantaṃ sutejasam |
na śaśāka bahiḥ kartuṃ ko'pi taṃ munisattama ||
3.34.d:
महाग्निमिव दुःस्पर्शं प्रज्वलन्तं सुतेजसम् ।
न शशाक बहिः कर्तुं कोऽपि तं मुनिसत्तम ॥
3.34.m: Like a great fire, unapproachable, blazing with immense splendor, / no one was able to cast him outside, O best of sages.

3.34.s:
tataḥ sa bhikṣukastāta nānālīlāviśāradaḥ |
darśayāmāsa śailāya svaprabhāvamanantakam ||
3.34.d:
ततः स भिक्षुकस्तात नानालीलाविशारदः ।
दर्शयामास शैलाय स्वप्रभावमनन्तकम् ॥
3.34.m: Then that beggar, O dear one, skilled in diverse sports, / revealed his endless power to the mountain.

3.34.s:
śailo dadarśa taṃ tatra viṣṇurūpadharaṃ drutam |
tato brahmasvarūpaṃ ca sūryarūpaṃ tataḥ kṣaṇāt ||
3.34.d:
शैलो ददर्श तं तत्र विष्णुरूपधरं द्रुतम् ।
ततो ब्रह्मस्वरूपं च सूर्यरूपं ततः क्षणात् ॥
3.34.m: The mountain beheld him there instantly assuming the form of Viṣṇu, / then the form of Brahmā, and in an instant the form of Sūrya.

3.34.s:
tato dadarśa taṃ tāta rudrarūpaṃ mahādbhutam |
pārvatīsahitaṃ ramyaṃ vihasantaṃ sutejasam ||
3.34.d:
ततो ददर्श तं तात रुद्ररूपं महाद्भुतम् ।
पार्वतीसहितं रम्यं विहसन्तं सुतेजसम् ॥
3.34.m: Then, O dear one, he saw him in the exceedingly wondrous form of Rudra, / accompanied by Pārvatī, delightful, smiling, and endowed with great splendor.

3.34.s:
evaṃ subahurūpāṇi tasya tatra dadarśa saḥ |
suvismito babhūvāśu paramānandasamplutaḥ ||
3.34.d:
एवं सुबहुरूपाणि तस्य तत्र ददर्श सः ।
सुविस्मितो बभूवाशु परमानन्दसम्प्लुतः ॥
3.34.m: Thus he beheld there his exceedingly numerous forms; / he was soon filled with wonder and flooded with supreme bliss.

3.34.s:
athāsau bhikṣuvaryo hi tasmāttasyāśca sūtikṛt |
bhikṣāṃ yayāce durgāṃ tāṃ nānyajjagrāha kiñcana ||
3.34.d:
अथासौ भिक्षुवर्यो हि तस्मात्तस्याश्च सूतिकृत् ।
भिक्षां ययाचे दुर्गां तां नान्यज्जग्राह किञ्चन ॥
3.34.m: Then that best of beggars, the creator of sport, / asked that Durgā as alms from him and from her; he accepted nothing else.

3.34.s:
tataścāntardadhe bhikṣusvarūpaḥ parameśvaraḥ |
svālayaṃ sa jagāmāśu durgāvākyapraṇoditaḥ ||
3.34.d:
ततश्चान्तर्दधे भिक्षुस्वरूपः परमेश्वरः ।
स्वालयं स जगामाशु दुर्गावाक्यप्रणोदितः ॥
3.34.m: Then Parameśvara in the form of the beggar vanished; / impelled by the words of Durgā, he quickly went to his own abode.

3.34.s:
tadā babhūva sujñānaṃ menāśaileśayorapi |
āvāṃ śivo vañcayitvā gatavānsvālayaṃ vibhuḥ ||
3.34.d:
तदा बभूव सुज्ञानं मेनाशैलेशयोरपि ।
आवां शिवो वञ्चयित्वा गतवान्स्वालयं विभुः ॥
3.34.m: Then true knowledge arose in Menā and the lord of mountains: / “The all-pervading Śiva has deceived us and gone to his own abode.

3.34.s:
asmai deyā svakanyeyaṃ pārvatī sutapasvinī |
evaṃ vicārya ca tayoḥ śive bhaktirabhūtparā ||
3.34.d:
अस्मै देया स्वकन्येयं पार्वती सुतपस्विनी ।
एवं विचार्य च तयोः शिवे भक्तिरभूत्परा ॥
3.34.m: Our daughter Pārvatī, rich in austerity, is to be given to him.” / Having thus reflected, supreme devotion to Śiva arose in them both.

3.34.s:
ato rudro mahotīśca kṛtvā bhaktamudāvaham |
vivāhaṃ kṛtavānprītyā pārvatyā sa vidhānataḥ ||
3.34.d:
अतो रुद्रो महोतीश्च कृत्वा भक्तमुदावहम् ।
विवाहं कृतवान्प्रीत्या पार्वत्या स विधानतः ॥
3.34.m: Therefore Rudra, having performed sports that brought joy to his devotees, / lovingly and according to the rules married Pārvatī.

3.34.s:
iti proktastu te tāta sunartakanaṭāhvayaḥ |
śivāvatāro hi mayā śivāvākyaprapūrakaḥ ||
3.34.d:
इति प्रोक्तस्तु ते तात सुनर्तकनटाह्वयः ।
शिवावतारो हि मया शिवावाक्यप्रपूरकः ॥
3.34.m: Thus, O dear one, I have told you of Śiva’s incarnation / named Sunartakanaṭa, which fulfilled the words of Śivā.

3.34.s:
idamākhyānamanaghaṃ paramaṃ vyāhṛtaṃ mayā |
ya etacchṛṇuyātprītyā sa sukhī gatimāpnuyāt ||
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ||
śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
śrīśivamahāpurāṇam ||
tṛtīyāyāṃ śatarudrasaṃhitāyāṃ
3.34.d:
इदमाख्यानमनघं परमं व्याहृतं मया ।
य एतच्छृणुयात्प्रीत्या स सुखी गतिमाप्नुयात् ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः ॥
श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ॥
तृतीयायां शतरुद्रसंहितायां
3.34.m:
This supreme, faultless narrative has been recited by me; / whoever hears it with devotion shall become happy and attain the goal.

Thus ends the thirty-fourth chapter, titled “The Description of Śiva’s Incarnation as Sunartakanaṭa,” in the Śatarudrasaṃhitā, the third section of the Śrīśivamahāpurāṇa.

3.35.s:
nandīśvara uvāca |
sanatkumāra sarvajña śivasya paramātmanaḥ |
avatāraṃ śṛṇu vibhoḥ sādhuveṣadvijāhvayam ||
3.35.d:
नन्दीश्वर उवाच ।
सनत्कुमार सर्वज्ञ शिवस्य परमात्मनः ।
अवतारं शृणु विभोः साधुवेषद्विजाह्वयम् ॥
3.35.m: Nandīśvara said: / O omniscient Sanatkumāra, hear of the incarnation of the all-pervading Śiva, / the Supreme Self, named the Twice-Born in the Garb of an Ascetic.

3.35.s:
menāhimālayorbhaktiṃ śive jñātvā mahottamām |
cintāmāpuḥ surāḥ sarve mantrayāmāsurādarāt ||
3.35.d:
मेनाहिमालयोर्भक्तिं शिवे ज्ञात्वा महोत्तमाम् ।
चिन्तामापुः सुराः सर्वे मन्त्रयामासुरादरात् ॥
3.35.m: Knowing the most excellent devotion to Śiva in Menā and Himālaya, / all the gods became worried and respectfully deliberated:

3.35.s:
ekāntabhaktyā śailaścetkanyāṃ dāsyati śambhave |
dhruvaṃ nirvāṇatāṃ sadyaḥ samprāpsyati śivasya vai ||
3.35.d:
एकान्तभक्त्या शैलश्चेत्कन्यां दास्यति शम्भवे ।
ध्रुवं निर्वाणतां सद्यः सम्प्राप्स्यति शिवस्य वै ॥
3.35.m: “If the mountain gives his daughter to Śambhu with exclusive devotion, / he will surely immediately attain the state of liberation of Śiva.

3.35.s:
anantaratnādhāro'sau cetprayāsyati mokṣatām |
ratnagarbhābhidhā bhūmirmithyaiva bhavitā dhruvam ||
3.35.d:
अनन्तरत्नाधारोऽसौ चेत्प्रयास्यति मोक्षताम् ।
रत्नगर्भाभिधा भूमिर्मिथ्यैव भविता ध्रुवम् ॥
3.35.m: If he, the repository of endless jewels, attains liberation, / the name of the earth as ‘holding jewels in her womb’ will surely become false.

3.35.s:
sthāvaratvaṃ parityajya divyarūpaṃ vidhāya saḥ |
kanyāṃ śūlabhṛte dattvā śivalokaṃ gamiṣyati ||
3.35.d:
स्थावरत्वं परित्यज्य दिव्यरूपं विधाय सः ।
कन्यां शूलभृते दत्त्वा शिवलोकं गमिष्यति ॥
3.35.m: Abandoning immobility and assuming a divine form, / he will give his daughter to the trident-bearer and go to the world of Śiva.

3.35.s:
mahādevasya sārūpyaṃ prāpya śambhoranugrahāt |
tatra bhuktvā mahābhogāṃstato mokṣamavāpsyati ||
3.35.d:
महादेवस्य सारूप्यं प्राप्य शम्भोरनुग्रहात् ।
तत्र भुक्त्वा महाभोगांस्ततो मोक्षमवाप्स्यति ॥
3.35.m: Attaining similarity of form with Mahādeva by the grace of Śambhu, / he will enjoy great pleasures there and then attain liberation.”

3.35.s:
ityālocya surāḥ sarve jagmurgurugṛhaṃ mune |
cakrurnivedanaṃ gatvā gurave svārthasādhakāḥ ||
3.35.d:
इत्यालोच्य सुराः सर्वे जग्मुर्गुरुगृहं मुने ।
चक्रुर्निवेदनं गत्वा गुरवे स्वार्थसाधकाः ॥
3.35.m: Having thus reflected, all the gods went to their guru’s house, O sage; / having gone, those seekers of their own interest made a petition to the guru.

3.35.s:
devā ūcuḥ |
guro himālayagṛhaṃ gacchāsmatkāryasiddhaye |
kṛtvā nindāṃ maheśasya giribhaktiṃ nivāraya ||
3.35.d:
देवा ऊचुः ।
गुरो हिमालयगृहं गच्छास्मत्कार्यसिद्धये ।
कृत्वा निन्दां महेशस्य गिरिभक्तिं निवारय ॥
3.35.m: The gods said: / O guru, go to Himālaya’s house for the accomplishment of our purpose; / speaking ill of Maheśa, prevent the mountain’s devotion.

3.35.s:
svaśraddhayā sutāṃ dattvā śivāya sa girirguro |
labheta muktimatraiva dharaṇyāṃ sa hi tiṣṭhatu ||
3.35.d:
स्वश्रद्धया सुतां दत्त्वा शिवाय स गिरिर्गुरो ।
लभेत मुक्तिमत्रैव धरण्यां स हि तिष्ठतु ॥
3.35.m: If that mountain gives his daughter to Śiva with his faith, O guru, / he would attain liberation; let him rather remain right here on the earth.

3.35.s: iti devavacaḥ śrutvā provāca ca vicārya tān ||
3.35.d: इति देववचः श्रुत्वा प्रोवाच च विचार्य तान् ॥
3.35.m: Having heard those words of the gods and reflected, he spoke to them:

3.35.s:
gururuvāca |
kaścinmadhye ca yuṣmākaṃ gacchecchailāntikaṃ surāḥ |
sampādayetsvābhimatamahaṃ tatkartumakṣamaḥ ||
3.35.d:
गुरुरुवाच ।
कश्चिन्मध्ये च युष्माकं गच्छेच्छैलान्तिकं सुराः ।
सम्पादयेत्स्वाभिमतमहं तत्कर्तुमक्षमः ॥
3.35.m: The guru said: / Let someone among you go to the mountain, O gods, / and accomplish what is desired; I am unable to do that.

3.35.s:
athavā gacchata surā brahmalokaṃ savāsavāḥ |
tasmai vṛttaṃ kathaya svaṃ sa vaḥ kāryaṃ kariṣyati ||
3.35.d:
अथवा गच्छत सुरा ब्रह्मलोकं सवासवाः ।
तस्मै वृत्तं कथय स्वं स वः कार्यं करिष्यति ॥
3.35.m: Or else, O gods, go along with Indra to the world of Brahmā; / tell him your situation, and he will carry out your business.

3.35.s:
nandīśvara uvāca |
tacchrutvā te samālocya jagmurvidhisabhāṃ surāḥ |
sarvaṃ nivedayāmāsustadvṛttaṃ purato vidheḥ ||
3.35.d:
नन्दीश्वर उवाच ।
तच्छ्रुत्वा ते समालोच्य जग्मुर्विधिसभां सुराः ।
सर्वं निवेदयामासुस्तद्वृत्तं पुरतो विधेः ॥
3.35.m: Nandīśvara said: / Having heard that and deliberated, the gods went to the assembly of the Creator; / they reported that whole situation before the Creator.

3.35.s:
avocattānvidhiḥ śrutvā tadvacaḥ suvicintya vai |
nāhaṃ kariṣye tannindāṃ duḥkhadāṃ kaharāṃ sadā ||
3.35.d:
अवोचत्तान्विधिः श्रुत्वा तद्वचः सुविचिन्त्य वै ।
नाहं करिष्ये तन्निन्दां दुःखदां कहरां सदा ॥
3.35.m: Having heard their words and carefully considered them, the Creator spoke to them: / “I will not speak ill of him, which always brings sorrow and destroys happiness.

3.35.s:
surā gacchata kailāsaṃ santoṣayata śaṅkaram |
prasthāpayata taṃ devaṃ himālayagṛhaṃ prati ||
3.35.d:
सुरा गच्छत कैलासं सन्तोषयत शङ्करम् ।
प्रस्थापयत तं देवं हिमालयगृहं प्रति ॥
3.35.m: Go to Kailāsa, O gods, and please Śaṅkara; / send that god himself toward the house of Himālaya.

3.35.s:
sa gacchedatha śaileśamātmanindāṃ karotu vai |
paranindā vināśāya svanindā yaśase matā ||
3.35.d:
स गच्छेदथ शैलेशमात्मनिन्दां करोतु वै ।
परनिन्दा विनाशाय स्वनिन्दा यशसे मता ॥
3.35.m: Let him go to the lord of mountains and speak ill of himself; / speaking ill of others is considered to cause ruin, while speaking ill of oneself brings renown.”

3.35.s:
nandīśvara uvāca |
tataste prayayuḥ śīghraṃ kailāsaṃ nikhilāḥ surāḥ |
supraṇamya śivaṃ bhaktyā tadvṛttaṃ nikhilā jaguḥ ||
3.35.d:
नन्दीश्वर उवाच ।
ततस्ते प्रययुः शीघ्रं कैलासं निखिलाः सुराः ।
सुप्रणम्य शिवं भक्त्या तद्वृत्तं निखिला जगुः ॥
3.35.m: Nandīśvara said: / Then all those gods went quickly to Kailāsa; / bowing low with devotion to Śiva, they related that entire situation.

3.35.s:
tacchrutvā devavacanaṃ svīcakāra maheśvaraḥ |
devānsuyāpayāmāsa tānāśvāsya vihasya saḥ ||
3.35.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा देववचनं स्वीचकार महेश्वरः ।
देवान्सुयापयामास तानाश्वास्य विहस्य सः ॥
3.35.m: Having heard the words of the gods, Maheśvara agreed; / having reassured them and laughed, he dismissed the gods.

3.35.s:
tataḥ sa bhagavāñchambhurmaheśo bhaktavatsalaḥ |
gantumaicchacchailamūlaṃ māyeśo na vikāravān ||
3.35.d:
ततः स भगवाञ्छम्भुर्महेशो भक्तवत्सलः ।
गन्तुमैच्छच्छैलमूलं मायेशो न विकारवान् ॥
3.35.m: Then the blessed Śambhu, Maheśa, affectionate toward devotees, / the lord of māyā, free from modification, wished to go to the base of the mountain.

3.35.s:
daṇḍī chatrī divyavāsā bibhrattilakamujjvalam |
kare sphaṭikamālāṃ ca śālagrāmaṃ gale dadhat ||
3.35.d:
दण्डी छत्री दिव्यवासा बिभ्रत्तिलकमुज्ज्वलम् ।
करे स्फटिकमालां च शालग्रामं गले दधत् ॥
3.35.m: Carrying a staff and an umbrella, clad in divine clothes, wearing a bright sectarian mark, / with a crystal rosary in his hand and bearing a śālagrāma on his neck,

3.35.s:
japannāma harerbhaktyā sādhuveṣadharo dvijaḥ |
himācalaṃ jagāmāśu bandhuvargaiḥ sarmanvitam ||
3.35.d:
जपन्नाम हरेर्भक्त्या साधुवेषधरो द्विजः ।
हिमाचलं जगामाशु बन्धुवर्गैः सर्मन्वितम् ॥
3.35.m: Reciting the name of Hari with devotion, the twice-born in the garb of an ascetic / went swiftly to Himācala, surrounded by his kinsmen.

3.35.s:
taṃ ca dṛṣṭvā samuttasthau sagaṇo'pi himālayaḥ |
nanāma daṇḍavadbhūmau sāṣṭāṅgaṃ vidhipūrvakam ||
3.35.d:
तं च दृष्ट्वा समुत्तस्थौ सगणोऽपि हिमालयः ।
ननाम दण्डवद्भूमौ साष्टाङ्गं विधिपूर्वकम् ॥
3.35.m: Seeing him, the Himalaya stood up with his attendants / and bowed full-length on the ground according to rule.

3.35.s:
tataḥ papraccha śaileśastaṃ dvijaṃ ko bhavāniti |
uvāca śīghraṃ viprendraḥ sa yogyadriṃ mahādarāt ||
3.35.d:
ततः पप्रच्छ शैलेशस्तं द्विजं को भवानिति ।
उवाच शीघ्रं विप्रेन्द्रः स योग्यद्रिं महादरात् ॥
3.35.m: Then the lord of mountains asked that twice-born, “Who are you?” / That best of brahmins immediately replied to the suitable mountain with great respect:

3.35.s:
sādhudvija uvāca |
sādhudvijāhvaḥ śailāhaṃ vaiṣṇavaḥ paramārthadṛk |
paropakārī sarvajñaḥ sarvagāmī gurorbalāt ||
3.35.d:
साधुद्विज उवाच ।
साधुद्विजाह्वः शैलाहं वैष्णवः परमार्थदृक् ।
परोपकारी सर्वज्ञः सर्वगामी गुरोर्बलात् ॥
3.35.m: The twice-born ascetic said: / “O mountain, I am called the twice-born ascetic, a Vaiṣṇava who sees the highest truth, / benevolent to others, omniscient, travelling everywhere by the power of my guru.

3.35.s:
mayā jñātaṃ svavijñānātsvasthāne śailasattama |
tacchṛṇu prītito vacmi hitvā dambhaṃ tavāntikam ||
3.35.d:
मया ज्ञातं स्वविज्ञानात्स्वस्थाने शैलसत्तम ।
तच्छृणु प्रीतितो वच्मि हित्वा दम्भं तवान्तिकम् ॥
3.35.m: O best of mountains, I learned [this] through my own insight in my own abode. / Listen to it; discarding deceit, I speak it to you out of affection.

3.35.s:
śaṅkarāya sutāṃ dātuṃ tvamicchasi nijodbhavām |
imāṃ padmāsamāṃ ramyāmajñātakulaśīline ||
3.35.d:
शङ्कराय सुतां दातुं त्वमिच्छसि निजोद्भवाम् ।
इमां पद्मासमां रम्यामज्ञातकुलशीलिने ॥
3.35.m: You wish to give your own-born daughter, / this lovely girl equal to Padmā, to Śaṅkara whose family and conduct are unknown.

3.35.s:
iyaṃ matiste śailendra na yuktā maṅgalapradā |
nibodha jñānināṃ śreṣṭha nārāyaṇakulodbhava ||
3.35.d:
इयं मतिस्ते शैलेन्द्र न युक्ता मङ्गलप्रदा ।
निबोध ज्ञानिनां श्रेष्ठ नारायणकुलोद्भव ॥
3.35.m: This notion of yours, O king of mountains, is not proper or auspicious. / Consider, O best of the wise, born in the lineage of Nārāyaṇa!

3.35.s:
paśya śailādhipatvaṃ ca na tasyaiko'sti bāndhavaḥ |
bāndhavānsvānprayatnena pṛccha menāṃ ca svapriyām ||
3.35.d:
पश्य शैलाधिपत्वं च न तस्यैकोऽस्ति बान्धवः ।
बान्धवान्स्वान्प्रयत्नेन पृच्छ मेनां च स्वप्रियाम् ॥
3.35.m: Look, O ruler of mountains! He does not have a single relative. / Ask your own kinsmen with care, and your beloved Menā.

3.35.s:
sarvānsampṛccha yatnena menādīnpārvatīṃ vinā |
rogiṇe nauṣadhaṃ śaila kupathyaṃ rocate sadā ||
3.35.d:
सर्वान्सम्पृच्छ यत्नेन मेनादीन्पार्वतीं विना ।
रोगिणे नौषधं शैल कुपथ्यं रोचते सदा ॥
3.35.m: Ask everyone carefully, beginning with Menā, except for Pārvatī. / To a sick man, O mountain, unwholesome food always tastes pleasing, not medicine.

3.35.s:
na te pātrānurūpaśca pārvatīdānakarmaṇi |
mahājanaḥ smeramukhaḥ śrutimātrādbhaviṣyati ||
3.35.d:
न ते पात्रानुरूपश्च पार्वतीदानकर्मणि ।
महाजनः स्मेरमुखः श्रुतिमात्राद्भविष्यति ॥
3.35.m: And he is not a suitable recipient for the act of giving Pārvatī away. / Great people will smile [in ridicule] merely upon hearing of it.

3.35.s:
nirāśrayaḥ sadāsaṅgo virūpo nirguṇo'vyayaḥ |
smaśānavāsī vikaṭo vyālagrāhī digambaraḥ ||
3.35.d:
निराश्रयः सदासङ्गो विरूपो निर्गुणोऽव्ययः ।
स्मशानवासी विकटो व्यालग्राही दिगम्बरः ॥
3.35.m: He is without shelter, ever unattached, deformed, devoid of qualities, immutable, / a dweller in cremation grounds, monstrous, a snake-catcher, naked,

3.35.s:
vibhūtibhūṣaṇo vyālavarāveṣṭitamastakaḥ |
sarvāśramaparibhraṣṭastvavijñātagatissadā ||
3.35.d:
विभूतिभूषणो व्यालवरावेष्टितमस्तकः ।
सर्वाश्रमपरिभ्रष्टस्त्वविज्ञातगतिस्सदा ॥
3.35.m: adorned with ashes, his head wrapped by supreme serpents, / fallen from all stages of life, and his course ever unknown.”

3.35.s:
brahmovāca |
ityādyuktvā vacastathyaṃ śivanindāparaṃ sa hi |
jagāma svālayaṃ śīghraṃ nānālīlākaraḥ śivaḥ ||
3.35.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
इत्याद्युक्त्वा वचस्तथ्यं शिवनिन्दापरं स हि ।
जगाम स्वालयं शीघ्रं नानालीलाकरः शिवः ॥
3.35.m: Brahmā said: / Having spoken such words intent on reviling Śiva, / Śiva, who performs various sports, swiftly departed to his own abode.

3.35.s:
tacchrutvā vipravacanamabhūtāṃ ca tanū tayoḥ |
viparītānarthapare kiṃ kariṣyāvahe dhruvam ||
3.35.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा विप्रवचनमभूतां च तनू तयोः ।
विपरीतानर्थपरे किं करिष्यावहे ध्रुवम् ॥
3.35.m: Hearing that word of the brahmin, the bodies of both [parents] / were confounded by the reverse disaster: “What shall we surely do?”

3.35.s:
tato rudro mahotiṃ ca kṛtvā bhaktamudāvahām |
vivāhayitvā girijāṃ devakāryaṃ cakāra saḥ ||
3.35.d:
ततो रुद्रो महोतिं च कृत्वा भक्तमुदावहाम् ।
विवाहयित्वा गिरिजां देवकार्यं चकार सः ॥
3.35.m: Then Rudra, having arranged a great festival that brought joy to his devotees / and having married the mountain's daughter, accomplished the work of the gods.

3.35.s:
iti proktastu te tāta sādhuveṣo dvijāhvayaḥ |
śivāvatāro hi mayā devakāryakaraḥ prabho ||
3.35.d:
इति प्रोक्तस्तु ते तात साधुवेषो द्विजाह्वयः ।
शिवावतारो हि मया देवकार्यकरः प्रभो ॥
3.35.m: Thus, O dear one, the incarnation of Śiva in the guise of an ascetic named a twice-born, / who accomplished the work of the gods, has been narrated to you by me, O lord.

3.35.s:
idamākhyānamanaghaṃ svargyamāyuṣyamuttamam |
yaḥ paṭhecchṛṇuyādvāpi sa sukhī gatimāpnuyāt ||
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ||
śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
śrīśivamahāpurāṇam ||
tṛtīyāyāṃ śatarudrasaṃhitāyāṃ
3.35.d:
इदमाख्यानमनघं स्वर्ग्यमायुष्यमुत्तमम् ।
यः पठेच्छृणुयाद्वापि स सुखी गतिमाप्नुयात् ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः ॥
श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ॥
तृतीयायां शतरुद्रसंहितायां
3.35.m:
Whoever recites or even listens to this sinless narrative, / which grants heaven and prolongs life, being happy, will attain the supreme state.

Thus ends the twenty-fifth chapter, entitled 'Description of the Incarnation of Śiva as the Twice-born Ascetic,' in the third book, the Śatarudrasaṃhitā, of the glorious Śiva Mahāpurāṇa.

3.36.s:
nandīśvara uvāca |
sanatkumāra sarvajña śivasya paramātmanaḥ |
avatāraṃ śṛṇu vibhoraśvatthāmāhvayaṃ param ||
3.36.d:
नन्दीश्वर उवाच ।
सनत्कुमार सर्वज्ञ शिवस्य परमात्मनः ।
अवतारं शृणु विभोरश्वत्थामाह्वयं परम् ॥
3.36.m: Nandīśvara said: / “O omniscient Sanatkumāra, hear about the supreme incarnation of the all-pervading lord, / Śiva the Supreme Self, known by the name Aśvatthāman.

3.36.s:
bṛhaspatermahābuddherdevarṣeraṃśato mune |
bharadvājātsamutpanno droṇo'yonija ātmavān ||
3.36.d:
बृहस्पतेर्महाबुद्धेर्देवर्षेरंशतो मुने ।
भरद्वाजात्समुत्पन्नो द्रोणोऽयोनिज आत्मवान् ॥
3.36.m: Born from Bharadvāja through a portion of Bṛhaspati, the seer among gods of great intellect, / was self-restrained Droṇa, not born from a womb, O sage.

3.36.s:
dhanurbhṛtāṃ varaḥ śūro viprarṣiḥ sarvaśāstravit |
bṛhatkīrtirmahātejā yaḥ sarvāstraviduttamaḥ ||
3.36.d:
धनुर्भृतां वरः शूरो विप्रर्षिः सर्वशास्त्रवित् ।
बृहत्कीर्तिर्महातेजा यः सर्वास्त्रविदुत्तमः ॥
3.36.m: He was the foremost of archers, a hero, a brahmin seer who knew all scriptures, / possessing great fame and immense splendour, the best knower of all weapons,

3.36.s:
dhanurvede ca vede ca niṣṇātaṃ yaṃ vidurbudhāḥ |
variṣṭhaṃ citrakarmāṇaṃ droṇaṃ svakulavardhanam ||
3.36.d:
धनुर्वेदे च वेदे च निष्णातं यं विदुर्बुधाः ।
वरिष्ठं चित्रकर्माणं द्रोणं स्वकुलवर्धनम् ॥
3.36.m: whom the wise knew to be skilled in both the science of archery and the Veda, / most eminent, performing wondrous deeds, Droṇa who increased his own lineage.

3.36.s:
kauravāṇāṃ sa ācarya āsītsvabalato dvija |
mahārathiṣu vikhyātaḥ ṣaṭsu kauravamadhyataḥ ||
3.36.d:
कौरवाणां स आचर्य आसीत्स्वबलतो द्विज ।
महारथिषु विख्यातः षट्सु कौरवमध्यतः ॥
3.36.m: He became the teacher of the Kauravas by his own power, O twice-born, / and was renowned among the six great chariot-warriors in the midst of the Kauravas.

3.36.s:
sāhāyyārthaṃ kauravāṇāṃ sa tepe vipulaṃ tapaḥ |
śivamuddiśya putrārthaṃ droṇācāryo dvijottamaḥ ||
3.36.d:
साहाय्यार्थं कौरवाणां स तेपे विपुलं तपः ।
शिवमुद्दिश्य पुत्रार्थं द्रोणाचार्यो द्विजोत्तमः ॥
3.36.m: For the sake of aiding the Kauravas, and for a son, / that best of the twice-born, Droṇācārya, performed vast austerity directed towards Śiva.

3.36.s:
tataḥ prasanno bhagavācchaṅkaro bhaktavatsalaḥ |
āvirbabhūva purato droṇasya munisattama ||
3.36.d:
ततः प्रसन्नो भगवाच्छङ्करो भक्तवत्सलः ।
आविर्बभूव पुरतो द्रोणस्य मुनिसत्तम ॥
3.36.m: Then, being pleased, the lord Śaṅkara, affectionate toward devotees, / appeared before Droṇa, O best of sages.

3.36.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā sa dvijo droṇastuṣṭāvāśu praṇamya tam |
mahāprasannahṛdayo natakaḥ sukṛtāñjaliḥ ||
3.36.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा स द्विजो द्रोणस्तुष्टावाशु प्रणम्य तम् ।
महाप्रसन्नहृदयो नतकः सुकृताञ्जलिः ॥
3.36.m: Seeing him, that twice-born Droṇa bowed down and praised him at once, / his heart exceedingly joyful, bowing low with hands respectfully folded.

3.36.s:
tasya stutyā ca tapasā santuṣṭaḥ śaṅkaraḥ prabhuḥ |
varaṃ brūhīti covāca droṇaṃ taṃ bhaktavatsalaḥ ||
3.36.d:
तस्य स्तुत्या च तपसा सन्तुष्टः शङ्करः प्रभुः ।
वरं ब्रूहीति चोवाच द्रोणं तं भक्तवत्सलः ॥
3.36.m: Pleased by his hymn of praise and austerity, the lord Śaṅkara, / affectionate toward devotees, said to that Droṇa: 'Choose a boon.'

3.36.s:
tacchrutvā śambhuvacanaṃ droṇaḥ prāhātha sannataḥ |
svāṃśajaṃ tanayaṃ dehi sarvājeyaṃ mahābalam ||
3.36.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा शम्भुवचनं द्रोणः प्राहाथ सन्नतः ।
स्वांशजं तनयं देहि सर्वाजेयं महाबलम् ॥
3.36.m: Hearing that word of Śambhu, Droṇa, bowed low, then said: / 'Grant me a son born of your own portion, invincible to all and of immense might.'

3.36.s:
tacchrutvā droṇavacanaṃ śambhuḥ proce tathāstviti |
abhūdantarhitastāta kautukī sukhakṛnmune ||
3.36.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा द्रोणवचनं शम्भुः प्रोचे तथास्त्विति ।
अभूदन्तर्हितस्तात कौतुकी सुखकृन्मुने ॥
3.36.m: Hearing that speech of Droṇa, Śambhu said, 'So be it.' / The playful one who grants happiness vanished, O dear sage.

3.36.s:
droṇo'pagacchatsvaṃ dhāma mahāhṛṣṭo gatabhramaḥ |
svapatnyai kathayāmāsa tadvṛtaṃ sakalaṃ mudā ||
3.36.d:
द्रोणोऽपगच्छत्स्वं धाम महाहृष्टो गतभ्रमः ।
स्वपत्न्यै कथयामास तद्वृतं सकलं मुदा ॥
3.36.m: Droṇa returned to his own home, exceedingly delighted and free of perplexity, / and joyfully recounted that entire occurrence to his wife.

3.36.s:
athāvasaramāsādya rudraḥ sarvāntakaḥ prabhuḥ |
svāṃśena tanayo jajñe droṇasya sa mahābalaḥ ||
3.36.d:
अथावसरमासाद्य रुद्रः सर्वान्तकः प्रभुः ।
स्वांशेन तनयो जज्ञे द्रोणस्य स महाबलः ॥
3.36.m: Then, finding the opportune time, the lord Rudra, the ender of all, / was born by his own portion as the son of Droṇa, possessed of immense might.

3.36.s:
aśvatthāmeti vikhyātaḥ sa babhūva kṣitau mune |
pravīraḥ kañjapatrākṣaḥ śatrupakṣakṣayaṅkaraḥ ||
3.36.d:
अश्वत्थामेति विख्यातः स बभूव क्षितौ मुने ।
प्रवीरः कञ्जपत्राक्षः शत्रुपक्षक्षयङ्करः ॥
3.36.m: He became renowned on earth as Aśvatthāman, O sage, / a hero, with eyes like lotus petals, who brought ruin to the enemy's side.

3.36.s:
yo bhārate raṇe khyātaḥ piturājñāmavāpya ca |
sahāyakṛd babhūvāta kauravāṇāṃ mahābalaḥ ||
3.36.d:
यो भारते रणे ख्यातः पितुराज्ञामवाप्य च ।
सहायकृद् बभूवात कौरवाणां महाबलः ॥
3.36.m: He, of immense might, renowned in the Bhārata battle, / having received the command of his father, became a helper of the Kauravas.

3.36.s:
yamāśritya mahāvīraṃ kauravāḥ sumahābalāḥ |
bhīṣmādayo babhūvuste'jeyā api divaukasām ||
3.36.d:
यमाश्रित्य महावीरं कौरवाः सुमहाबलाः ।
भीष्मादयो बभूवुस्तेऽजेया अपि दिवौकसाम् ॥
3.36.m: Relying on him, that great hero, the Kauravas of immense might, / Bhīṣma and the others, became invincible even to the gods.

3.36.s:
yadbhayātpāṇḍavāḥ sarve kauravāñjetumakṣamāḥ |
āsannaṣṭā mahāvīrā api sarve ca kovidāḥ ||
3.36.d:
यद्भयात्पाण्डवाः सर्वे कौरवाञ्जेतुमक्षमाः ।
आसन्नष्टा महावीरा अपि सर्वे च कोविदाः ॥
3.36.m: Out of fear of him, all the Pāṇḍavas were unable to defeat the Kauravas; / though all were great heroes and skilled, they were rendered helpless.

3.36.s:
kṛṣṇopadeśataḥ śambhostapaḥ kṛtvātidāruṇam |
prāpya cāstraṃ śambhuvarājjigye tānarjunastataḥ ||
3.36.d:
कृष्णोपदेशतः शम्भोस्तपः कृत्वातिदारुणम् ।
प्राप्य चास्त्रं शम्भुवराज्जिग्ये तानर्जुनस्ततः ॥
3.36.m: Following Kṛṣṇa's instruction, having performed very fierce austerity toward Śambhu / and obtained a weapon by Śambhu's boon, Arjuna then defeated them.

3.36.s:
aśvatthāmā mahāvīro mahādevāṃśajo mune |
tathāpi tadbhaktivaśaḥ svapratāpamadarśayat ||
3.36.d:
अश्वत्थामा महावीरो महादेवांशजो मुने ।
तथापि तद्भक्तिवशः स्वप्रतापमदर्शयत् ॥
3.36.m: Aśvatthāman was a great hero born of a portion of Mahādeva, O sage; / nevertheless, subject to devotion to him, he displayed his own prowess,

3.36.s:
vināśya pāṇḍavasutān śikṣitānapi yatnataḥ |
kṛṣṇādibhirmahāvīrairanivāryabalaḥ paraiḥ ||
3.36.d:
विनाश्य पाण्डवसुतान् शिक्षितानपि यत्नतः ।
कृष्णादिभिर्महावीरैरनिवार्यबलः परैः ॥
3.36.m: having destroyed the sons of the Pāṇḍavas, even though carefully trained / by Kṛṣṇa and other great heroes, he possessing irresistible power against his enemies.

3.36.s:
putraśokena vikalamāpatantaṃ tamarjunam |
rathenācyutavantaṃ hi dṛṣṭvā sa ca parādravat ||
3.36.d:
पुत्रशोकेन विकलमापतन्तं तमर्जुनम् ।
रथेनाच्युतवन्तं हि दृष्ट्वा स च पराद्रवत् ॥
3.36.m: Seeing that Arjuna, distraught with grief for his sons, / rushing forward with Acyuta on his chariot, he fled.

3.36.s:
astraṃ brahmaśiro nāma taduparyasṛjatsa hi |
tataḥ prādurabhūttejaḥ pracaṇḍaṃ sarvato diśam ||
3.36.d:
अस्त्रं ब्रह्मशिरो नाम तदुपर्यसृजत्स हि ।
ततः प्रादुरभूत्तेजः प्रचण्डं सर्वतो दिशम् ॥
3.36.m: He released the weapon named Brahmaśiras against him; / then a fierce radiance burst forth in every direction.

3.36.s:
prāṇāpadamabhiprekṣya so'rjunaḥ kleśasaṃyutaḥ |
uvāca kṛṣṇaṃ viklānto naṣṭatejā mahābhayaḥ ||
3.36.d:
प्राणापदमभिप्रेक्ष्य सोऽर्जुनः क्लेशसंयुतः ।
उवाच कृष्णं विक्लान्तो नष्टतेजा महाभयः ॥
3.36.m: Seeing danger to his life and filled with distress, / that Arjuna, exhausted, his energy lost and in great fear, spoke to Kṛṣṇa:

3.36.s:
arjuna uvāca |
kimidaṃ svitkuto veti kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa na vedmyaham |
sarvatomukhamāyāti tejaścedaṃ sudussaham ||
3.36.d:
अर्जुन उवाच ।
किमिदं स्वित्कुतो वेति कृष्ण कृष्ण न वेद्म्यहम् ।
सर्वतोमुखमायाति तेजश्चेदं सुदुस्सहम् ॥
3.36.m: Arjuna said: / 'What is this, or whence comes it, O Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa? I do not know. / And this unbearable brilliance is advancing in every direction.'

3.36.s:
nandīśvara uvāca |
śrutvārjunavacaścedaṃ sa kṛṣṇaḥ śaivasattamaḥ |
dadhyau śivaṃ sadāraṃ ca pratyāhārjunamādarāt ||
3.36.d:
नन्दीश्वर उवाच ।
श्रुत्वार्जुनवचश्चेदं स कृष्णः शैवसत्तमः ।
दध्यौ शिवं सदारं च प्रत्याहार्जुनमादरात् ॥
3.36.m: Nandīśvara said: / Hearing this word of Arjuna, Kṛṣṇa, that best of Śaivas, / meditated upon Śiva together with his consort and respectfully answered Arjuna:

3.36.s:
śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca |
vetthedaṃ droṇaputrasya brāhmamastraṃ maholbaṇam |
na hyasyānyatamaṃ kiñcidastraṃ pratyavakarśanam ||
3.36.d:
श्रीकृष्ण उवाच ।
वेत्थेदं द्रोणपुत्रस्य ब्राह्ममस्त्रं महोल्बणम् ।
न ह्यस्यान्यतमं किञ्चिदस्त्रं प्रत्यवकर्शनम् ॥
3.36.m: The glorious Kṛṣṇa said: / 'Know this to be the formidable Brahma-weapon of the son of Droṇa; / indeed, there is no other weapon whatsoever to counter it.

3.36.s:
śivaṃ smara drutaṃ śambhuṃ svaprabhuṃ bhaktarakṣakam |
yena dattaṃ hi te svāstraṃ sarvakāryakaraṃ param ||
3.36.d:
शिवं स्मर द्रुतं शम्भुं स्वप्रभुं भक्तरक्षकम् ।
येन दत्तं हि ते स्वास्त्रं सर्वकार्यकरं परम् ॥
3.36.m: Remember quickly Śiva, Śambhu, your own lord, the protector of devotees, / by whom was given to you his supreme weapon that accomplishes all purposes.'”

3.36.s:
jahyastrateja unnaddhaṃ tvaṃ tacchaivāstratejasā |
ityuktvā ca svayaṃ kṛṣṇaḥ śivaṃ dadhyau tadarthakaḥ ||
3.36.d:
जह्यस्त्रतेज उन्नद्धं त्वं तच्छैवास्त्रतेजसा ।
इत्युक्त्वा च स्वयं कृष्णः शिवं दध्यौ तदर्थकः ॥
3.36.m: "Destroy that raised power of the weapon through the power of Śiva's weapon." / Having spoken thus, Kṛṣṇa himself meditated on Śiva for that purpose.

3.36.s:
tacchrutvā kṛṣṇavacanaṃ pārthaḥ smṛtvā śivaṃ hṛdi |
spṛṣṭvāpastaṃ praṇamyāśu cikṣepāstraṃ tato mune ||
3.36.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा कृष्णवचनं पार्थः स्मृत्वा शिवं हृदि ।
स्पृष्ट्वापस्तं प्रणम्याशु चिक्षेपास्त्रं ततो मुने ॥
3.36.m: Hearing that speech of Kṛṣṇa, Pārtha remembered Śiva in his heart, / touched water, quickly bowed to him, and then discharged his weapon, O sage.

3.36.s:
yadyapyastraṃ brahmaśirastvamoghaṃ cāpratikriyam |
śaivāstratejasā sadyaḥ samaśāmyanmahāmune ||
3.36.d:
यद्यप्यस्त्रं ब्रह्मशिरस्त्वमोघं चाप्रतिक्रियम् ।
शैवास्त्रतेजसा सद्यः समशाम्यन्महामुने ॥
3.36.m: Even though that weapon, the Brahmaśiras, was unfailing and irresistible, / it was immediately pacified by the power of Śiva's weapon, O great sage.

3.36.s:
mā maṃsthā hyetadāścaryaṃ sarvacitramaye śive |
yaḥ svaśaktyākhilaṃ viśvaṃ sṛjatyavati hantyajaḥ ||
3.36.d:
मा मंस्था ह्येतदाश्चर्यं सर्वचित्रमये शिवे ।
यः स्वशक्त्याखिलं विश्वं सृजत्यवति हन्त्यजः ॥
3.36.m: Indeed, you should not consider this a wonder in Śiva, who consists of all wonders, / the unborn who by his own power creates, protects, and destroys the entire universe.

3.36.s:
aśvatthāmā tato jñātvā vṛttametacchivāṃśajaḥ |
śaivaṃ na vivyathe kiñcicchivecchātuṣṭadhīrmune ||
3.36.d:
अश्वत्थामा ततो ज्ञात्वा वृत्तमेतच्छिवांशजः ।
शैवं न विव्यथे किञ्चिच्छिवेच्छातुष्टधीर्मुने ॥
3.36.m: Then Aśvatthāman, born of a portion of Śiva, learning of this event / relating to Śiva, was not pained at all, his mind satisfied with Śiva's will, O sage.

3.36.s:
atha drauṇiridaṃ viśvaṃ kṛtsnaṃ kartumapāṇḍavam |
uttarāgarbhagaṃ bālaṃ nāśituṃ mana ādadhe ||
3.36.d:
अथ द्रौणिरिदं विश्वं कृत्स्नं कर्तुमपाण्डवम् ।
उत्तरागर्भगं बालं नाशितुं मन आदधे ॥
3.36.m: Then the son of Droṇa set his mind to destroy the child residing in Uttarā's womb, / in order to make this entire world bereft of Pāṇḍavas.

3.36.s:
brahmāstramanivāryaṃ tadanyairastrairmahāprabham |
uttarāgarbhamuddiśya cikṣepa sa mahāprabhuḥ ||
3.36.d:
ब्रह्मास्त्रमनिवार्यं तदन्यैरस्त्रैर्महाप्रभम् ।
उत्तरागर्भमुद्दिश्य चिक्षेप स महाप्रभुः ॥
3.36.m: He, the mighty lord, discharged the brahmāstra, irresistible / by other weapons and of great radiance, directing it toward Uttarā's womb.

3.36.s:
tataśca sottarā jiṣṇuvadhūrvikalamānasā |
kṛṣṇaṃ tuṣṭāva lakṣmīśaṃ dahyamānā tadastrataḥ ||
3.36.d:
ततश्च सोत्तरा जिष्णुवधूर्विकलमानसा ।
कृष्णं तुष्टाव लक्ष्मीशं दह्यमाना तदस्त्रतः ॥
3.36.m: And then that Uttarā, the bride of Jiṣṇu, her mind agitated, / praised Kṛṣṇa, the lord of Lakṣmī, as she was being burned by that weapon.

3.36.s:
tataḥ kṛṣṇaḥ śivaṃ dhyātvā hṛdā nutvā praṇamya ca |
apāṇḍavamidaṃ kartuṃ drauṇerastramabudhyata ||
3.36.d:
ततः कृष्णः शिवं ध्यात्वा हृदा नुत्वा प्रणम्य च ।
अपाण्डवमिदं कर्तुं द्रौणेरस्त्रमबुध्यत ॥
3.36.m: Then Kṛṣṇa, having meditated on Śiva, praised him in his heart, and bowed, / understood that the weapon of the son of Droṇa was meant to render this [world] bereft of Pāṇḍavas.

3.36.s:
svarakṣārthendradattena tadastreṇa suvarcasā |
sudarśanena tasyāśca vyadhādrakṣāṃ śivājñayā ||
3.36.d:
स्वरक्षार्थेन्द्रदत्तेन तदस्त्रेण सुवर्चसा ।
सुदर्शनेन तस्याश्च व्यधाद्रक्षां शिवाज्ञया ॥
3.36.m: By command of Śiva, through that weapon of great brilliance given by Indra for his own protection, / the Sudarśana, he effected her protection.

3.36.s:
svarūpaṃ śaṅkarādeśātkṛtaṃ śaivavareṇa ha |
kṛṣṇena caritaṃ jñātvā vimanaskaḥ śanairabhūt ||
3.36.d:
स्वरूपं शङ्करादेशात्कृतं शैववरेण ह ।
कृष्णेन चरितं ज्ञात्वा विमनस्कः शनैरभूत् ॥
3.36.m: The manifestation had indeed been made by Kṛṣṇa, the best of Śaivas, by command of Śaṅkara; / learning of the deed, he gradually became downcast in mind.

3.36.s:
tataḥ sa kṛṣṇaḥ prītātmā pāṇḍavānsakalānapi |
apātayattadaṅghryostu tuṣṭaye tasya śaivarāṭ ||
3.36.d:
ततः स कृष्णः प्रीतात्मा पाण्डवान्सकलानपि ।
अपातयत्तदङ्घ्र्योस्तु तुष्टये तस्य शैवराट् ॥
3.36.m: Then that Kṛṣṇa, his heart pleased, made all the Pāṇḍavas / fall at his feet, in order to propitiate him, the king of Śaivas.

3.36.s:
atha drauṇiḥ prasannātmā pāṇḍavānkṛṣṇameva ca |
nānāvarāndadau prītyā so'śvatthāmānugṛhya ca ||
3.36.d:
अथ द्रौणिः प्रसन्नात्मा पाण्डवान्कृष्णमेव च ।
नानावरान्ददौ प्रीत्या सोऽश्वत्थामानुगृह्य च ॥
3.36.m: Then the son of Droṇa, pleased at heart, showing grace to the Pāṇḍavas / and to Kṛṣṇa, that Aśvatthāman affectionately gave various boons.

3.36.s:
itthaṃ maheśvarastāta cakre līlāṃ parāṃ prabhuḥ |
avatīrya kṣitau drauṇirūpeṇa munisattama ||
3.36.d:
इत्थं महेश्वरस्तात चक्रे लीलां परां प्रभुः ।
अवतीर्य क्षितौ द्रौणिरूपेण मुनिसत्तम ॥
3.36.m: Thus, O dear one, the Lord, Maheśvara, performed his supreme sport, / having descended upon the earth in the form of the son of Droṇa, O best of sages.

3.36.s:
śivāvatāro'śvatthāmā mahābalaparākramaḥ |
trailokyasukhado'dyāpi vartate jāhnavītaṭe ||
3.36.d:
शिवावतारोऽश्वत्थामा महाबलपराक्रमः ।
त्रैलोक्यसुखदोऽद्यापि वर्तते जाह्नवीतटे ॥
3.36.m: The incarnation of Śiva, Aśvatthāman, of great strength and valor, / bestowing happiness upon the three worlds, resides even today on the bank of the Jāhnavī.

3.36.s:
aśvatthāmāvatāraste varṇitaḥ śaṅkaraprabhoḥ |
sarvasiddhikaraścāpi bhaktābhīṣṭaphalapradaḥ ||
3.36.d:
अश्वत्थामावतारस्ते वर्णितः शङ्करप्रभोः ।
सर्वसिद्धिकरश्चापि भक्ताभीष्टफलप्रदः ॥
3.36.m: The incarnation of Lord Śaṅkara as Aśvatthāman has been described to you; / it brings about all accomplishments and grants the fruit of the desires of devotees.

3.36.s:
ya idaṃ śṛṇuyādbhaktyā kīrtayedvā samāhitaḥ |
sa siddhiṃ prāpnuyādiṣṭāmante śivapuraṃ vrajet ||
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ||
śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
śrīśivamahāpurāṇam ||
tṛtīyāyāṃ śatarudrasaṃhitāyāṃ
3.36.d:
य इदं शृणुयाद्भक्त्या कीर्तयेद्वा समाहितः ।
स सिद्धिं प्राप्नुयादिष्टामन्ते शिवपुरं व्रजेत् ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः ॥
श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ॥
तृतीयायां शतरुद्रसंहितायां
3.36.m:
Whoever hears this with devotion or recites it with a collected mind / will attain the desired accomplishment, and at the end go to the city of Śiva.

Thus ends the thirty-sixth chapter, named 'The Description of Śiva's Incarnation as Aśvatthāman,' in the Śatarudrasaṃhitā, the third [book] of the auspicious Śiva Mahāpurāṇa.

3.37.s:
nandīśvara uvāca |
śṛṇu prājña kirātākhyamavatāraṃ pinākinaḥ |
mūkaṃ ca hatavānprīto yo'rjunāya varaṃ dadau ||
3.37.d:
नन्दीश्वर उवाच ।
शृणु प्राज्ञ किराताख्यमवतारं पिनाकिनः ।
मूकं च हतवान्प्रीतो योऽर्जुनाय वरं ददौ ॥
3.37.m: Nandīśvara said: / Listen, O wise one, to the incarnation called Kirāta of the wielder of the Pināka, / who, having killed Mūka, was pleased and granted a boon to Arjuna.

3.37.s:
suyodhanajitāste vai pāṇḍavāḥ pravarāśca te |
draupadyā ca tayā sādhvyā dvaitākhyaṃ vanamāyayuḥ ||
3.37.d:
सुयोधनजितास्ते वै पाण्डवाः प्रवराश्च ते ।
द्रौपद्या च तया साध्व्या द्वैताख्यं वनमाययुः ॥
3.37.m: Those preeminent Pāṇḍavas, conquered by Suyodhana, / went with that virtuous Draupadī to the forest named Dvaita.

3.37.s:
tatraiva sūryadattāṃ vai sthālīṃ cāśritya te tadā |
kālaṃ ca vāhayāmāsuḥ sukhena kila pāṇḍavāḥ ||
3.37.d:
तत्रैव सूर्यदत्तां वै स्थालीं चाश्रित्य ते तदा ।
कालं च वाहयामासुः सुखेन किल पाण्डवाः ॥
3.37.m: Relying there upon the cooking vessel given by the Sun, / the Pāṇḍavas indeed spent their time happily.

3.37.s:
chalārthaṃ preritastena durvāsā munipuṅgavaḥ |
suyodhanena viprendra pāṇḍavāntikamādarāt ||
3.37.d:
छलार्थं प्रेरितस्तेन दुर्वासा मुनिपुङ्गवः ।
सुयोधनेन विप्रेन्द्र पाण्डवान्तिकमादरात् ॥
3.37.m: The eminent sage Durvāsas was sent by that Suyodhana / with deceitful intent, O best of brahmins, into the presence of the Pāṇḍavas with [feigned] respect.

3.37.s:
chātraiḥ svairvāyutaiḥ sārdhaṃ yayāce tatra tānmudā |
bhojyaṃ cittepsitaṃ vai sa tebhyaścaiva samāgataḥ ||
3.37.d:
छात्रैः स्वैर्वायुतैः सार्धं ययाचे तत्र तान्मुदा ।
भोज्यं चित्तेप्सितं वै स तेभ्यश्चैव समागतः ॥
3.37.m: Together with ten thousand of his students, he arrived / and gladly requested food desired by his heart from them.

3.37.s:
svīkṛtya pāṇḍavaistaistaiḥ snānārthaṃ preṣitāstadā |
durvāsaḥpramukhāścaiva munayaśca tapasvinaḥ ||
3.37.d:
स्वीकृत्य पाण्डवैस्तैस्तैः स्नानार्थं प्रेषितास्तदा ।
दुर्वासःप्रमुखाश्चैव मुनयश्च तपस्विनः ॥
3.37.m: Having consented, those Pāṇḍavas then sent Durvāsas / and the other sages, the ascetics, to bathe.

3.37.s:
atha te pāṇḍavāḥ sarve annābhāvānmunīśvara |
duḥkhitāśca tadā prāṇāṃstyaktuṃ citte samādadhuḥ ||
3.37.d:
अथ ते पाण्डवाः सर्वे अन्नाभावान्मुनीश्वर ।
दुःखिताश्च तदा प्राणांस्त्यक्तुं चित्ते समादधुः ॥
3.37.m: Then all those Pāṇḍavas, O lord among sages, for lack of food, / were distressed and resolved in their minds to give up their lives.

3.37.s:
draupadyā ca smṛtaḥ kṛṣṇa āgatastatkṣaṇādapi |
śākaṃ ca bhakṣayitvā tu teṣāṃ tṛptiṃ samādadhat ||
3.37.d:
द्रौपद्या च स्मृतः कृष्ण आगतस्तत्क्षणादपि ।
शाकं च भक्षयित्वा तु तेषां तृप्तिं समादधत् ॥
3.37.m: Remembered by Draupadī, Kṛṣṇa arrived that very instant, / and having eaten a vegetable leaf, he brought them satisfaction.

3.37.s:
durvāsāśca tadā śiṣyāṃstṛptān jñātvā yayau punaḥ |
pāṇḍavāḥ kṛcchranirmuktāḥ kṛṣṇasya kṛpayā tadā ||
3.37.d:
दुर्वासाश्च तदा शिष्यांस्तृप्तान् ज्ञात्वा ययौ पुनः ।
पाण्डवाः कृच्छ्रनिर्मुक्ताः कृष्णस्य कृपया तदा ॥
3.37.m: Then Durvāsas, finding his disciples satisfied, went away again; / the Pāṇḍavas were freed from distress by the grace of Kṛṣṇa at that time.

3.37.s:
atha te pāṇḍavāḥ kṛṣṇaṃ papracchuḥ kiṃ bhaviṣyati |
balavān śatrurutpannaḥ kiṃ kāryaṃ tadvada prabho ||
3.37.d:
अथ ते पाण्डवाः कृष्णं पप्रच्छुः किं भविष्यति ।
बलवान् शत्रुरुत्पन्नः किं कार्यं तद्वद प्रभो ॥
3.37.m: Then those Pāṇḍavas asked Kṛṣṇa: "What will happen? / A powerful enemy has arisen; tell us what is to be done, O Lord."

3.37.s:
nandīśvara uvāca |
iti pṛṣṭhastadā taistu śrīkṛṣṇaḥ pāṇḍavairmune |
smṛtvā śivapadāmbhojau pāṇḍavānidamabravīt ||
3.37.d:
नन्दीश्वर उवाच ।
इति पृष्ठस्तदा तैस्तु श्रीकृष्णः पाण्डवैर्मुने ।
स्मृत्वा शिवपदाम्भोजौ पाण्डवानिदमब्रवीत् ॥
3.37.m: Nandīśvara said: / Thus questioned at that time by those Pāṇḍavas, O sage, / Śrī Kṛṣṇa, remembering the lotus feet of Śiva, spoke this to the Pāṇḍavas:

3.37.s:
śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca |
śrūyatāṃ pāṇḍavāḥ śreṣṭhāḥ śrutvā kartavyameva hi |
madvṛttāntaṃ viśeṣeṇa śivasevāsamanvitam ||
3.37.d:
श्रीकृष्ण उवाच ।
श्रूयतां पाण्डवाः श्रेष्ठाः श्रुत्वा कर्तव्यमेव हि ।
मद्वृत्तान्तं विशेषेण शिवसेवासमन्वितम् ॥
3.37.m: Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: / "Listen, O best of Pāṇḍavas; having heard, it should indeed be done: / my own account in particular, which is connected with the service of Śiva.

3.37.s:
dvārakāṃ ca mayā gatvā śatrūṇāṃ vijigīṣayā |
vicārya copadeśāṃśca hyupamanyormahātmanaḥ ||
3.37.d:
द्वारकां च मया गत्वा शत्रूणां विजिगीषया ।
विचार्य चोपदेशांश्च ह्युपमन्योर्महात्मनः ॥
3.37.m: Having gone to Dvārakā with the desire to conquer enemies, / and having reflected upon the instructions of the great-souled Upamanyu,

3.37.s:
mayā hyārādhitaḥ śambhuḥ prasannaḥ parameśvaraḥ |
baṭuke parvataśreṣṭhe saptamāsaṃ susevitaḥ ||
3.37.d:
मया ह्याराधितः शम्भुः प्रसन्नः परमेश्वरः ।
बटुके पर्वतश्रेष्ठे सप्तमासं सुसेवितः ॥
3.37.m: Śambhu, Parameśvara, was propitiated by me and became pleased; / he was well served for seven months on the excellent mountain Baṭuka.

3.37.s:
iṣṭānkāmānadānmahyaṃ viśveśaśca svayaṃ sthitaḥ |
tatprabhāvānmayā sarvasāmarthyaṃ labdhamuttamam ||
3.37.d:
इष्टान्कामानदान्मह्यं विश्वेशश्च स्वयं स्थितः ।
तत्प्रभावान्मया सर्वसामर्थ्यं लब्धमुत्तमम् ॥
3.37.m: The Lord of the Universe, standing in person, granted me my cherished desires; / through his power, all supreme capability was obtained by me.

3.37.s:
idānīṃ sevyate devo bhuktimuktiphalapradaḥ |
yūyaṃ sevata taṃ śambhumapi sarvasukhāvaham ||
3.37.d:
इदानीं सेव्यते देवो भुक्तिमुक्तिफलप्रदः ।
यूयं सेवत तं शम्भुमपि सर्वसुखावहम् ॥
3.37.m: Now that God, who grants the fruits of enjoyment and liberation, is being served; / you too should serve that Śambhu, who brings all happiness."

3.37.s:
nandīśvara uvāca |
ityuktvāntardadhe kṛṣṇa āśvāsyātha ca pāṇḍavān |
dvārakāmagamacchīghraṃ smaran śivapadāmbujam ||
3.37.d:
नन्दीश्वर उवाच ।
इत्युक्त्वान्तर्दधे कृष्ण आश्वास्याथ च पाण्डवान् ।
द्वारकामगमच्छीघ्रं स्मरन् शिवपदाम्बुजम् ॥
3.37.m: Nandīśvara said: / Having spoken thus, Kṛṣṇa consoled the Pāṇḍavas and disappeared; / he went quickly to Dvārakā, remembering the lotus feet of Śiva.

3.37.s:
pāṇḍavā atha bhillaṃ ca preṣayāmāsurojasā |
guṇānāṃ ca parīkṣārthaṃ tasya duryodhanasya ca ||
3.37.d:
पाण्डवा अथ भिल्लं च प्रेषयामासुरोजसा ।
गुणानां च परीक्षार्थं तस्य दुर्योधनस्य च ॥
3.37.m: Then the Pāṇḍavas swiftly sent a mountaineer / in order to examine the merits of that Duryodhana.

3.37.s:
so'pi sarvaṃ ca tatratyaṃ duryodhanaguṇodayam |
samīcīnaṃ ca tajjñātvā punaḥ prāpa prabhūnprati ||
3.37.d:
सोऽपि सर्वं च तत्रत्यं दुर्योधनगुणोदयम् ।
समीचीनं च तज्ज्ञात्वा पुनः प्राप प्रभून्प्रति ॥
3.37.m: He, too, learning all about Duryodhana's rise in virtue there / to be proper, returned to his masters.

3.37.s:
taduktaṃ te niśamyaivaṃ duḥkhaṃ prāpurmunīśvara |
parasparaṃ samūcuste pāṇḍavā atiduḥkhitāḥ ||
3.37.d:
तदुक्तं ते निशम्यैवं दुःखं प्रापुर्मुनीश्वर ।
परस्परं समूचुस्ते पाण्डवा अतिदुःखिताः ॥
3.37.m: Having heard what he said, they were filled with grief, O lord among sages; / those Pāṇḍavas, exceedingly grieved, spoke to one another:

3.37.s:
kiṃ kartavyaṃ kva gantavyamasmābhiradhunā yudhi |
samarthā api vai sarve satyapāśena yantritāḥ ||
3.37.d:
किं कर्तव्यं क्व गन्तव्यमस्माभिरधुना युधि ।
समर्था अपि वै सर्वे सत्यपाशेन यन्त्रिताः ॥
3.37.m: "What should be done? Where should we go now in battle? / Though all capable, we are restrained by the fetter of truth."

3.37.s:
nandīśvara uvāca |
etasminsamaye vyāso bhasmabhūṣitamastakaḥ |
rudrākṣābharaṇaścāyājjaṭājūṭavibhūṣitaḥ ||
3.37.d:
नन्दीश्वर उवाच ।
एतस्मिन्समये व्यासो भस्मभूषितमस्तकः ।
रुद्राक्षाभरणश्चायाज्जटाजूटविभूषितः ॥
3.37.m: Nandīśvara said: / At this time Vyāsa arrived, his head adorned with ashes, / ornamented with rudrākṣa beads, and adorned with a matted coil of hair,

3.37.s:
pañcākṣaraṃ japanmantraṃ śivapremasamākulaḥ |
tejasāṃ ca svayaṃrāśiḥ sākṣāddharma ivāparaḥ ||
3.37.d:
पञ्चाक्षरं जपन्मन्त्रं शिवप्रेमसमाकुलः ।
तेजसां च स्वयंराशिः साक्षाद्धर्म इवापरः ॥
3.37.m: muttering the five-syllable mantra, overwhelmed with love for Śiva, / himself a mass of radiant energy, like Dharma incarnate.

3.37.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā te tadā prītā utthāya purataḥ sthitāḥ |
dattvāsanaṃ tadā tasmai kuśājinasuśobhitam ||
3.37.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा ते तदा प्रीता उत्थाय पुरतः स्थिताः ।
दत्त्वासनं तदा तस्मै कुशाजिनसुशोभितम् ॥
3.37.m: Seeing him then, delighted, they stood up before him; / having offered him a seat beautified with kuśa grass and an antelope skin,

3.37.s:
tatropaviṣṭaṃ taṃ vyāsaṃ pūjayanti sma harṣitāḥ |
stutiṃ ca vividhāṃ kṛtvā dhanyāḥ sma iti vādinaḥ ||
3.37.d:
तत्रोपविष्टं तं व्यासं पूजयन्ति स्म हर्षिताः ।
स्तुतिं च विविधां कृत्वा धन्याः स्म इति वादिनः ॥
3.37.m: joyfully they worshiped that Vyāsa who was seated there; / and having offered diverse praises, they said, 'We are blessed!'

3.37.s:
tapaścaiva susantaptaṃ dānāni vividhāni ca |
tatsarvaṃ saphalaṃ jātaṃ tṛptāste darśanātprabho ||
3.37.d:
तपश्चैव सुसन्तप्तं दानानि विविधानि च ।
तत्सर्वं सफलं जातं तृप्तास्ते दर्शनात्प्रभो ॥
3.37.m: "The austerities well performed and the diverse gifts given— / all that has borne fruit; they are satisfied by the sight of you, O Lord."

3.37.s:
duḥkhaṃ ca dūrato jātaṃ darśanātte pitāmaha |
duṣṭaiścaiva mahāduḥkhaṃ dattaṃ naḥ krūrakarmabhiḥ ||
3.37.d:
दुःखं च दूरतो जातं दर्शनात्ते पितामह ।
दुष्टैश्चैव महादुःखं दत्तं नः क्रूरकर्मभिः ॥
3.37.m: And our suffering has been driven far away through seeing you, O grandfather. / Great suffering indeed was inflicted on us by the wicked perpetrators of cruel deeds.

3.37.s:
śrīmatāṃ darśane jāte duḥkhaṃ caiva gamiṣyati |
kadācinna gataṃ tatra niścayo'yaṃ vicāritaḥ ||
3.37.d:
श्रीमतां दर्शने जाते दुःखं चैव गमिष्यति ।
कदाचिन्न गतं तत्र निश्चयोऽयं विचारितः ॥
3.37.m: When the glorious are seen, suffering surely vanishes; / if it ever did not vanish, that matter has been carefully considered [by us].

3.37.s:
mahatāmāśrame prāpte samarthe sarvakarmaṇi |
yadi duḥkhaṃ na gacchettu daivamevātra kāraṇam ||
3.37.d:
महतामाश्रमे प्राप्ते समर्थे सर्वकर्मणि ।
यदि दुःखं न गच्छेत्तु दैवमेवात्र कारणम् ॥
3.37.m: When one reaches the hermitage of the great, who are capable in all actions, / if suffering still does not leave, then destiny alone is the cause here.

3.37.s:
niścayenaiva gacchettu dāridyaṃ duḥkhakāraṇam |
mahatāṃ ca svabhāvo'yaṃ kalpavṛkṣasamo mataḥ ||
3.37.d:
निश्चयेनैव गच्छेत्तु दारिद्यं दुःखकारणम् ।
महतां च स्वभावोऽयं कल्पवृक्षसमो मतः ॥
3.37.m: Certainly poverty, the cause of suffering, must depart; / for the nature of the great is regarded as equal to the wish-fulfilling tree.

3.37.s:
tadguṇāneva gaṇayanmahato vastumātrataḥ |
āśrayasya vaśādeva puṃso vai jāyate prabho ||
3.37.d:
तद्गुणानेव गणयन्महतो वस्तुमात्रतः ।
आश्रयस्य वशादेव पुंसो वै जायते प्रभो ॥
3.37.m: Reckoning those qualities from the mere reality of the great, / O Lord, [all things] arise for a person solely through the power of recourse [to them].

3.37.s:
laghutvaṃ ca mahattvaṃ ca nātra kāryā vicāraṇā |
uttamānāṃ svabhāvo'yaṃ yaddīnapratipālanam ||
3.37.d:
लघुत्वं च महत्त्वं च नात्र कार्या विचारणा ।
उत्तमानां स्वभावोऽयं यद्दीनप्रतिपालनम् ॥
3.37.m: Lowness or greatness—no doubt should be harbored in this matter; / for the nature of the noble is to protect the wretched.

3.37.s:
raṅkasya lakṣaṇaṃ loke hyatiśreyaskaraṃ matam |
puro'sya parayatno vai sujanānāṃ ca sevanam ||
3.37.d:
रङ्कस्य लक्षणं लोके ह्यतिश्रेयस्करं मतम् ।
पुरोऽस्य परयत्नो वै सुजनानां च सेवनम् ॥
3.37.m: The characteristic of the beggar in this world is held to bring the highest good: / first, he makes an effort to serve virtuous people.

3.37.s:
ataḥ paraṃ ca bhāgyaṃ vai doṣaścaiva na dīyatām |
etasmātkāraṇātsvāmiṃstvayi dṛṣṭo śubhaṃ tadā ||
3.37.d:
अतः परं च भाग्यं वै दोषश्चैव न दीयताम् ।
एतस्मात्कारणात्स्वामिंस्त्वयि दृष्टो शुभं तदा ॥
3.37.m: Beyond this lies good fortune; do not assign blame. / For this reason, O master, when you were seen, good fortune arose then.

3.37.s:
tvadāgamanamātreṇa santuṣṭāni manāṃsi naḥ |
diśopadeśaṃ yenāśu duḥkhaṃ naṣṭaṃ bhavecca naḥ ||
3.37.d:
त्वदागमनमात्रेण सन्तुष्टानि मनांसि नः ।
दिशोपदेशं येनाशु दुःखं नष्टं भवेच्च नः ॥
3.37.m: By your mere arrival, our minds have been gladdened. / Impart an instruction by which our suffering may quickly be destroyed.

3.37.s:
nandīśvara uvāca |
ityetadvacanaṃ śrutvā pāṇḍavānāṃ mahāmuniḥ |
prasannamānaso bhūtvā vyāsaścaivābravīdidam ||
3.37.d:
नन्दीश्वर उवाच ।
इत्येतद्वचनं श्रुत्वा पाण्डवानां महामुनिः ।
प्रसन्नमानसो भूत्वा व्यासश्चैवाब्रवीदिदम् ॥
3.37.m: Nandīśvara said: / Hearing this speech of the Pāṇḍavas, the great sage / Vyāsa, his mind pleased, spoke as follows:

3.37.s:
he pāṇḍavāśca yūyaṃ vai na kaṣṭaṃ kartumarhatha |
dhanyāḥ stha kṛtakṛtyāḥ stha satyaṃ naiva vilopitam ||
3.37.d:
हे पाण्डवाश्च यूयं वै न कष्टं कर्तुमर्हथ ।
धन्याः स्थ कृतकृत्याः स्थ सत्यं नैव विलोपितम् ॥
3.37.m: “O Pāṇḍavas, you ought not to give way to distress; / you are blessed, you have accomplished your duty, and truth has not been abandoned by you.

3.37.s:
sujanānāṃ svabhāvo'yaṃ prāṇānte'pi suśobhanaḥ |
dharmaṃ tyajanti naivātra satyaṃ saphalabhājanam ||
3.37.d:
सुजनानां स्वभावोऽयं प्राणान्तेऽपि सुशोभनः ।
धर्मं त्यजन्ति नैवात्र सत्यं सफलभाजनम् ॥
3.37.m: Such is the most radiant nature of good people, even at the end of life: / they do not abandon righteousness here, which is the vessel of fruitful truth.

3.37.s:
asmākaṃ caiva yūyaṃ ca te cāpi samatāṃ gatāḥ |
tathāpi pakṣapāto vai dharmiṣṭhānāṃ mato budhaiḥ ||
3.37.d:
अस्माकं चैव यूयं च ते चापि समतां गताः ।
तथापि पक्षपातो वै धर्मिष्ठानां मतो बुधैः ॥
3.37.m: To us, both you and they have achieved equality; / nevertheless, bias toward the righteous is approved by the wise.

3.37.s:
dhṛtarāṣṭrena duṣṭena prathamaṃ ca hyacakṣuṣā |
dharmastyaktaḥ svayaṃ lobhādyuṣmākaṃ rājyamāhṛtam ||
3.37.d:
धृतराष्ट्रेन दुष्टेन प्रथमं च ह्यचक्षुषा ।
धर्मस्त्यक्तः स्वयं लोभाद्युष्माकं राज्यमाहृतम् ॥
3.37.m: First, righteous duty was personally abandoned out of greed by the wicked and blind Dhṛtarāṣṭra, / and your kingdom was seized.

3.37.s:
tasya yūyaṃ ca te cāpi putrā eva na saṃśayaḥ |
pitaryaparate bālā anukampyā mahātmanaḥ ||
3.37.d:
तस्य यूयं च ते चापि पुत्रा एव न संशयः ।
पितर्यपरते बाला अनुकम्प्या महात्मनः ॥
3.37.m: Both you and they are indeed his sons, without doubt; / when the father passes away, the children of a great soul are worthy of pity.

3.37.s:
paścātputraśca tenaiva vārito na kadācana |
anartho naiva jāyeta yaccaivaṃ ca kṛtaṃ tadā ||
3.37.d:
पश्चात्पुत्रश्च तेनैव वारितो न कदाचन ।
अनर्थो नैव जायेत यच्चैवं च कृतं तदा ॥
3.37.m: Afterwards, his son was never restrained by him. / No calamity would have arisen if he had acted thus back then.

3.37.s:
ataḥ paraṃ ca yajjātaṃ tajjātaṃ nānyathā bhavet |
ayaṃ duṣṭo bhavantaśca dharmiṣṭhāḥ satyavādinaḥ ||
3.37.d:
अतः परं च यज्जातं तज्जातं नान्यथा भवेत् ।
अयं दुष्टो भवन्तश्च धर्मिष्ठाः सत्यवादिनः ॥
3.37.m: Beyond this, whatever has happened has happened; it cannot be otherwise. / That man is wicked, while you are righteous speakers of truth.

3.37.s:
tasmādante ca tasyaivāśubhaṃ hi bhavitā dhruvam |
yaccaiva vāpitaṃ bījaṃ tatpraroho bhavediha ||
3.37.d:
तस्मादन्ते च तस्यैवाशुभं हि भविता ध्रुवम् ।
यच्चैव वापितं बीजं तत्प्ररोहो भवेदिह ॥
3.37.m: Therefore, in the end, misfortune will certainly befall him; / for whatever seed is sown, that very sprout arises here.

3.37.s:
tasmādduḥkhaṃ na kartavyaṃ bhavadbhiḥ sarvathā dhruvam |
bhaviṣyati śubhaṃ vo hi nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ||
3.37.d:
तस्माद्दुःखं न कर्तव्यं भवद्भिः सर्वथा ध्रुवम् ।
भविष्यति शुभं वो हि नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥
3.37.m: Therefore, no sorrow at all should be felt by you; / good fortune will certainly come to you; no doubt should be harbored in this matter.”

3.37.s:
nandīśvara uvāca |
ityuktvā pāṇḍavāḥ sarve tena vyāsena prīṇitāḥ |
yudhiṣṭhiramukhāste ca punarevābruvanvacaḥ ||
3.37.d:
नन्दीश्वर उवाच ।
इत्युक्त्वा पाण्डवाः सर्वे तेन व्यासेन प्रीणिताः ।
युधिष्ठिरमुखास्ते च पुनरेवाब्रुवन्वचः ॥
3.37.m: Nandīśvara said: / Having spoken thus, all the Pāṇḍavas, comforted by that Vyāsa / and headed by Yudhiṣṭhira, again spoke these words:

3.37.s:
pāṇḍavā ūcuḥ |
satyamuktaṃ tvayā nātha duṣṭairduḥkhaṃ nirantaram |
duṣṭātmabhirvane cāpi dīyate hi muhurmuhuḥ ||
3.37.d:
पाण्डवा ऊचुः ।
सत्यमुक्तं त्वया नाथ दुष्टैर्दुःखं निरन्तरम् ।
दुष्टात्मभिर्वने चापि दीयते हि मुहुर्मुहुः ॥
3.37.m: The Pāṇḍavas said: / “O protector, you have spoken truly. Constant sorrow / is being inflicted again and again by the wicked-minded, even in the forest.

3.37.s:
tannāśayāśubhaṃ meṃ'dya kiñciddeyaṃ śubhaṃ vibho |
kṛṣṇena kathitaṃ pūrvamārādhyaḥ śaṅkaraḥ sadā ||
3.37.d:
तन्नाशयाशुभं मेंऽद्य किञ्चिद्देयं शुभं विभो ।
कृष्णेन कथितं पूर्वमाराध्यः शङ्करः सदा ॥
3.37.m: Therefore, destroy our misfortune today; grant us some good fortune, O powerful one. / Formerly, Kṛṣṇa told [us] that Śaṅkara is always to be worshipped.

3.37.s:
pramādaśca kṛto'smābhistadvacaḥ śithilīkṛtam |
sa devamārgastu punaridānīmupadiśyatām ||
3.37.d:
प्रमादश्च कृतोऽस्माभिस्तद्वचः शिथिलीकृतम् ।
स देवमार्गस्तु पुनरिदानीमुपदिश्यताम् ॥
3.37.m: Negligence was committed by us, and his word was neglected. / Let that divine path now be taught [to us] once again.”

3.37.s:
nandīśvara uvāca |
ityetadvacanaṃ śrutvā vyāso harṣasamanvitaḥ |
uvāca pāṇḍavānprītyā smṛtvā śivapadāmbujam ||
3.37.d:
नन्दीश्वर उवाच ।
इत्येतद्वचनं श्रुत्वा व्यासो हर्षसमन्वितः ।
उवाच पाण्डवान्प्रीत्या स्मृत्वा शिवपदाम्बुजम् ॥
3.37.m: Nandīśvara said: / Hearing this speech, Vyāsa, filled with joy, / lovingly addressed the Pāṇḍavas, remembering the lotus feet of Śiva.

3.37.s:
vyāsa uvāca |
śrūyatāṃ vacanaṃ me'dya pāṇḍavā dharmabuddhayaḥ |
satyamuktaṃ tu kṛṣṇena mayā saṃsevyate śivaḥ ||
3.37.d:
व्यास उवाच ।
श्रूयतां वचनं मेऽद्य पाण्डवा धर्मबुद्धयः ।
सत्यमुक्तं तु कृष्णेन मया संसेव्यते शिवः ॥
3.37.m: Vyāsa said: / “Listen to my word today, O Pāṇḍavas, whose minds are fixed on righteousness: / what Kṛṣṇa said is true, and Śiva is worshipped by me.

3.37.s:
bhavadbhiḥ sevyatāṃ prītyā sukhaṃ syādatulaṃ sadā |
sarvaduḥkhaṃ bhavatyeva śivāsevāta eva hi ||
3.37.d:
भवद्भिः सेव्यतां प्रीत्या सुखं स्यादतुलं सदा ।
सर्वदुःखं भवत्येव शिवासेवात एव हि ॥
3.37.m: Let him be served lovingly by you; peerless happiness will always follow. / All suffering indeed arises only from not serving Śiva.”

3.37.s:
nandīśvara uvāca |
atha pañcasu teṣveva vicārya śivapūjane |
arjunaṃ yogyamuccārya vyāso munivarastathā ||
3.37.d:
नन्दीश्वर उवाच ।
अथ पञ्चसु तेष्वेव विचार्य शिवपूजने ।
अर्जुनं योग्यमुच्चार्य व्यासो मुनिवरस्तथा ॥
3.37.m: Nandīśvara said: / Then, deliberating among those five regarding the worship of Śiva, / Vyāsa, the excellent sage, declared Arjuna to be worthy.

3.37.s:
tapaḥsthānaṃ vicāryaivaṃ tataḥ sa munisattamaḥ |
pāṇḍavāndharmasanniṣṭhānpunarevābravīdidam ||
3.37.d:
तपःस्थानं विचार्यैवं ततः स मुनिसत्तमः ।
पाण्डवान्धर्मसन्निष्ठान्पुनरेवाब्रवीदिदम् ॥
3.37.m: Having thus considered a place for austerity, that best of sages / spoke once again to the Pāṇḍavas, who were devoted to righteousness:

3.37.s:
vyāsa uvāca |
śrūyatāṃ pāṇḍavāḥ sarve kathayāmi hitaṃ sadā |
śivaṃ sarvaṃ paraṃ dṛṣṭvā paraṃ brahma satāṃ gatim ||
3.37.d:
व्यास उवाच ।
श्रूयतां पाण्डवाः सर्वे कथयामि हितं सदा ।
शिवं सर्वं परं दृष्ट्वा परं ब्रह्म सतां गतिम् ॥
3.37.m: Vyāsa said: / “Listen, all Pāṇḍavas; I speak what is always beneficial, / seeing Śiva as all, supreme, the highest Brahman, the refuge of the virtuous.

3.37.s:
brahmāditriparārddhāntaṃ yatkiñcid dṛśyate jagat |
tatsarvaṃ śivarūpaṃ ca pūjyaṃ dhyeyaṃ ca tatpunaḥ ||
3.37.d:
ब्रह्मादित्रिपरार्द्धान्तं यत्किञ्चिद् दृश्यते जगत् ।
तत्सर्वं शिवरूपं च पूज्यं ध्येयं च तत्पुनः ॥
3.37.m: Whatever world is seen, from Brahmā up to three parārdha intervals, / all that is the form of Śiva, and it should be worshipped and meditated upon.

3.37.s:
sarveṣāṃ caiva sevyo'sau śaṅkaraḥ sarvaduḥkhahā |
śivaḥ svalpena kālena samprasīdati bhaktitaḥ ||
3.37.d:
सर्वेषां चैव सेव्योऽसौ शङ्करः सर्वदुःखहा ।
शिवः स्वल्पेन कालेन सम्प्रसीदति भक्तितः ॥
3.37.m: And that Śaṅkara, the destroyer of all sorrow, is to be served by all; / Śiva is well pleased in a short time through devotion.

3.37.s:
suprasanno maheśo hi bhaktebhyaḥ sakalapradaḥ |
bhuktiṃ muktimihāmutra yacchatīti suniścitam ||
3.37.d:
सुप्रसन्नो महेशो हि भक्तेभ्यः सकलप्रदः ।
भुक्तिं मुक्तिमिहामुत्र यच्छतीति सुनिश्चितम् ॥
3.37.m: For the great lord, highly pleased, gives everything to his devotees; / it is certain that he bestows enjoyment and liberation here and in the hereafter.

3.37.s:
tasmātsevyaḥ sadā śabhbhurbhuktimuktiphalepsubhiḥ |
puruṣaḥ śaṅkaraḥ sākṣād dṛṣṭahantā satāṃ gatiḥ ||
3.37.d:
तस्मात्सेव्यः सदा शभ्भुर्भुक्तिमुक्तिफलेप्सुभिः ।
पुरुषः शङ्करः साक्षाद् दृष्टहन्ता सतां गतिः ॥
3.37.m: Therefore, Śambhu should always be served by those desiring the fruits of enjoyment and liberation: / the Primal Person Śaṅkara is visible, the destroyer [of sins], the refuge of the good.

3.37.s:
parantu prathamaṃ śakravidyāṃ dṛḍhamanā japet |
kṣatriyasya parākhyasya cedameva samāhitam ||
3.37.d:
परन्तु प्रथमं शक्रविद्यां दृढमना जपेत् ।
क्षत्रियस्य पराख्यस्य चेदमेव समाहितम् ॥
3.37.m: However, first one should recite with a firm mind the Indra-lore; / for a high-ranking kṣatriya, this alone is fitting.

3.37.s:
ato'rjunaśca prathamaṃ śakravidyāṃ japed dṛḍhaḥ |
kariṣyati parīkṣāṃ prāk santuṣṭastadbhaviṣyati ||
3.37.d:
अतोऽर्जुनश्च प्रथमं शक्रविद्यां जपेद् दृढः ।
करिष्यति परीक्षां प्राक् सन्तुष्टस्तद्भविष्यति ॥
3.37.m: Therefore, let Arjuna first recite the Indra-lore with firm resolve; / [Indra] will first test him, and then he will be satisfied.

3.37.s:
suprasannaśca vighnāni saṃhariṣyati sarvadā |
punaścaivaṃ śivasyaiva varaṃ mantraṃ pradāsyati ||
3.37.d:
सुप्रसन्नश्च विघ्नानि संहरिष्यति सर्वदा ।
पुनश्चैवं शिवस्यैव वरं मन्त्रं प्रदास्यति ॥
3.37.m: And when he is well pleased, he will always destroy obstacles, / and then he will impart the excellent mantra of Śiva.”

3.37.s:
nandīśvara uvāca |
ityuktvārjunamāhūyopendravidyāmupādiśat |
snātvā ca prāṅmukho bhūtvā jagrāhārjuna ugradhīḥ ||
3.37.d:
नन्दीश्वर उवाच ।
इत्युक्त्वार्जुनमाहूयोपेन्द्रविद्यामुपादिशत् ।
स्नात्वा च प्राङ्मुखो भूत्वा जग्राहार्जुन उग्रधीः ॥
3.37.m: Nandīśvara said: / Having spoken thus, calling Arjuna, he imparted the Upendra-lore. / Having bathed and faced east, Arjuna of fierce intellect received it.

3.37.s:
pārthivasya vidhānaṃ ca tasmai munivaro dadau |
pratyuvāca ca taṃ vyāso dhanañjayamudāradhīḥ ||
3.37.d:
पार्थिवस्य विधानं च तस्मै मुनिवरो ददौ ।
प्रत्युवाच च तं व्यासो धनञ्जयमुदारधीः ॥
3.37.m: And the excellent sage gave him the procedure for the earthen emblem; / then Vyāsa, of noble intellect, said to Dhanañjaya:

3.37.s:
vyāsa uvāca |
ito gacchādhunā pārtha indrakīle suśobhane |
jāhnavyāśca samīpe vai sthitvā samyak tapaḥ kuru ||
3.37.d:
व्यास उवाच ।
इतो गच्छाधुना पार्थ इन्द्रकीले सुशोभने ।
जाह्नव्याश्च समीपे वै स्थित्वा सम्यक् तपः कुरु ॥
3.37.m: Vyāsa said: / “Depart from here now, O Pārtha, to the most lovely Indrakīla, / and staying near the Jāhnavī, perform austerity properly.

3.37.s:
adṛśyā caiva vidyā syātsadā te hitakāriṇī |
ityāśiṣaṃ dadau tasmai tataḥ provāca tānmuniḥ ||
3.37.d:
अदृश्या चैव विद्या स्यात्सदा ते हितकारिणी ।
इत्याशिषं ददौ तस्मै ततः प्रोवाच तान्मुनिः ॥
3.37.m: May this lore remain invisible [to others] and always beneficial to you!” / Having thus given him his blessing, the sage then said to them:

3.37.s:
dharmamāsthāya sarve vai tiṣṭhantu nṛpasattamāḥ |
siddhiḥ syātsarvathā śreṣṭhā nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ||
3.37.d:
धर्ममास्थाय सर्वे वै तिष्ठन्तु नृपसत्तमाः ।
सिद्धिः स्यात्सर्वथा श्रेष्ठा नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥
